items.title: Spin dynamics and ortho–para conversion in $H_{2}O$ during the phase transition from gas to solid in external magnetic fields
items.summary: The spin dynamics of water ice in the presence of external magnetic fields are investigated. The employedmodel is based on the approach introduced by Buntkowsky et al. (2008), which considers two nearest-neighbor water molecules and yields a four-spin system, as the abundant oxygen isotope has zero nuclear spin.The model is extended to include coupling to external magnetic fields, allowing us to analyze the interplaybetween magnetic dipole–dipole interactions and magnetic field coupling. Two types of configurations areexamined: (i) static, homogeneous fields, corresponding to a time-independent interaction, and (ii) spatiallyvarying sinusoidal fields in relative motion with the molecules, leading to a time-dependent interaction.All computations are performed within the density operator formalism. The ortho/para populations and thetotal spin projections are evaluated during the first tens of milliseconds following the gas-to-solid phasetransition. For static homogeneous fields, we show that increasing field strength suppresses dipolar-induceddepolarization. Assuming that all molecules are initially in the para state, we show that static homogeneousfields can drive the ortho population up to approximately 50%, whereas suitably chosen sinusoidal-fieldconfigurations can increase it beyond 90%. These results are relevant for schemes aiming to preserve ormanipulate nuclear-spin polarization during deposition.
items.author: Chrysovalantis S. Kannis, Ralf Engels, Nicolas Faatz, Simon Pütz et al.

items.title: Data-Driven Voltage Control for Distribution Networks with High Penetration of PVs via Improved DDPG
items.summary: The highly increasing integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) has brought significant challenges for distribution network voltage control, which struggles with fast and stochastic fluctuations. This paper proposes a data-driven voltage control method utilizing an improved deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) to minimize power losses while maintaining voltage within a safe operating range. The data-driven voltage control framework is established first, with the controlling center formulated as the agent. Based on the distribution network system and the voltage control original model, the data-driven voltage control model is formulated via the Markov decision process (MDP). A voltage sensitivity-guided DDPG algorithm, which incorporates the voltage-reactive power injection sensitivity matrix into the actor policy gradient, is developed to embed physical grid knowledge and reduce the actor’s reliance on critic action-gradient estimates, thus the practicality and generalization of data-driven voltage control is improved. Numerical simulations on the modified IEEE 33-node test system show the method maintains all nodal voltages within limits and reduces total system losses under varying PV generation, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for future sustainable power systems.
items.author: Xiaolong Xiao, Linghao Zhang, Ziran Guo, Xiaoxing Lu et al.

items.title: Learning lattice parameters from powder X-ray diffraction data using invariants
items.summary: We present a machine learning (ML) method to determine unit-cell parameters from powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) data using a novel invariant lattice representation. In ML, the data representation used can have a substantial impact on the prediction quality. Previous approaches have directly predicted lattice parameters (a, b, c, α, β, γ) from XRD inputs. However, these parameters depend strongly on the unit-cell reduction or convention used. In this work, we construct an invariant representation of the reciprocal lattice that is independent of primitive-cell convention, based on the bispectrum - a descriptor built from spherical harmonic projections of lattice points. The calculation of the lattice bispectrum is differentiable, and we demonstrate how to invert it using gradient-based optimization initialized from a nearest-neighbor lookup. We show that, with a fixed ML model architecture, using the lattice bispectrum as the ML target rather than the unit-cell parameters leads to more accurate lattice parameter predictions. For example, using the MP-20 dataset, a subset of the Materials Project database, the bispectrum reduces length mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 11.08% to 2.43% and angle MAPE from 12.15% to 2.45% compared with direct prediction with the same model architecture. We additionally benchmark our approach against pre-existing XRD data to crystal structure models such as Crystalyze and assess its performance on experimental data. Beyond unit-cell representation, we anticipate this invariant lattice representation could serve more broadly as a geometry-aware target for other crystallographic ML tasks such as structure generation.
items.source: Acta Crystallographica Section A Foundations and Advances

items.title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A con-vergent mixed-methods investigation and the triadic care model
items.summary: While clinical guidelines strongly endorse psychologically informed physiotherapy (PIP) and cognitive-behavioral techniques (CBT) for musculoskeletal pain, routine clinical uptake remains inconsistent.Most implementation research describes clinician attitudes without modeling the cognitive and systemic mechanisms that impede translation into daily practice.This study investigates the "intention-behavior gap" in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation among Iranian physiotherapists using the COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation -Behavior) framework and introduces the Triadic Care Model as an operational solution.A convergent mixed-methods design (QUAN + QUAL) compliant with the Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study (GRAMMS) guidelines was conducted between 2023 and 2024.The quantitative phase surveyed 450 licensed physiotherapists using the validated Psychological Practice and Skills Tool (PPST).Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) tested hypothesized paths linking psychological self-efficacy, systemic barriers, postgraduate education, and clinical utilization.The qualitative phase comprised semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 20 practicing physiotherapists analyzed via reflexive thematic analysis.Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated via a joint display matrix.A pronounced intention-behavior gap was identified: 78.2% (n=352) of clinicians strongly endorsed the bio psychosocial model, yet only 24.4% (n=110) routinely implemented psychological techniques.SEM demonstrated excellent fit (χ2/df=2.15,CFI=.96,TLI=.95,RMSEA=.048[90% CI: .041-.055],SRMR=.042).Psychological self-efficacy directly predicted technique utilization (β=.41, p<.001), while postgraduate training indirectly enhanced utilization via self-efficacy (β=.34, p<.

items.title: Detection of Unmarked Non-Metallic Underground Pipelines Using Fine-Grained Strontium Ferrite-Based Powders
items.summary: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. Despite the advantages of non-metallic pipes, their use is associated with a number of specific problems characteristic of plastic materials. One of such significant problems facing the gas industry is the problem of detecting underground non-metallic utilities and selectively identifying them from adjacent facilities. Pipelines not linked to the global coordinate system in a timely manner can lead to significant economic costs in case of abnormal situations during construction and installation works. The paper investigates an original method of searching for non-metallic utilities associated with the introduction of magnetic powder into the gas flow. It is shown that in the case of the site location in the urban area it is a low-information and ambiguous method. On the contrary, in the open area, in the absence of third-party ferromagnetic interference, this method is not only potentially applicable, but deserves close attention and further research, for which the appropriate design of the test site is proposed. Potential application of the method will increase the informative value of data on the underground location of non-metallic pipelines by 15% for gas distribution pipelines of various diameters, considering the achievement of a magnetic induction level above the pipeline in the range of 60-120 nT.
items.author: I. S. Leonov, Gulnur Zakirova, A. V. Borisov, V. S. Borisova et al.

items.title: Understanding resonant inelastic X-ray scattering experiments of diazines via quantum dynamics simulation
items.summary: We present a combined theoretical and experimental study of the three diazine isomers pyrazine, pyrimidine, and pyridazine by means of resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) at the nitrogen K-edge, employing fully time-dependent quantum dynamics simulations to understand the role of nuclear motion in core-excited states. The RIXS process is simulated by wave-packet propagation in both the valence- and core-excited state manifolds, carried out with the (multilayer) multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree [(ML-)MCTDH] method. We use linear vibronic coupling Hamiltonians with up to 22 electronic states and compare a full-dimensional (24-mode) and a reduced six-mode model. We find good agreement between experiment and theory for all three molecules. In particular, our study highlights the essential role of nuclear motions during the population of short-lived intermediate core-excited states. Specifically, we show that ultrafast non-adiabatic transitions induce symmetry distortion that leads to additional emission bands, while interstate vibrational dynamics lead to vibrational progressions in the inelastic scattering spectra. These results establish a dynamical picture of the RIXS process in diazines that emphasises the importance of including nuclear dynamics in the calculations of resonant Raman processes.
items.author: Antonia Freibert, Sebastian Eckert, Vinícius Vaz da Cruz, Alexander Föhlisch et al.

items.title: EOM-fpCCSD: an accurate alternative to EOM-CCSD for doubly excited and charge-transfer states
items.summary: We introduce a new equation-of-motion coupled-cluster method based on a pair coupled-cluster doubles (pCCD) reference, termed frozen-pair EOM-CCSD (EOM-fpCCSD). This approach combines the computational efficiency of the pCCD ansatz with a dynamical correlation correction, enabling a reliable description of electronically excited states within the EOM framework. The method has been implemented in the open-source PyBEST software package. Its performance is systematically benchmarked against standard EOM-CCSD and its pair-tailored variant (EOM-ptCCSD), using both canonical Hartree-Fock and pCCD natural orbitals. For charge-transfer (CT) excitations taken from the QUEST database, EOM-fpCCSD yields excitation energies very close to those of EOM-CCSD, outperforming EOM-ptCCSD, as well as to the theoretical best estimates (TBEs). Working within the localized pCCD natural orbital basis allows us to determine the directed CT character, which quantifies the directed charge flow from one molecular domain to another. Numerical results show that EOM-fpCCSD, EOM-CCSD, and EOM-ptCCSD provide nearly identical descriptions of the directed CT character, despite changes in excitation energies. The true advantage of EOM-fpCCSD becomes evident for the challenging QUEST subset of doubly excited states. While EOM-ptCCSD performs similarly to standard EOM-CCSD, EOM-fpCCSD significantly outperforms both methods for these problematic states compared to TBEs. In addition to improving the accuracy of excitation energies, EOM-fpCCSD also converges for several states that standard EOM-CCSD and EOM-ptCCSD fail to converge. These results demonstrate that EOM-fpCCSD offers a promising and computationally efficient route toward a more accurate description of complex electronic excitations.
items.author: Katharina Bogusławski, Paweł Tecmer

items.title: Spectrally resolved X-ray scattering
items.summary: the inelastic transition matrix elements. By effectively merging spectroscopy and scattering, a time-resolved measurement of the molecular Bethe surface during a chemical reaction could reveal details of the reaction path through the manifolds of electronic states and conical intersections. However, conventional imaging detectors used for X-ray scattering lack energy resolution. We demonstrate here how the Bethe surface can be measured with the help of a spectral filter in the form of a thin zinc metal foil inserted between the target and the detector. Harnessing the inherent stochasticity of X-ray pulses generated by self-amplified spontaneous emission at X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs), we demonstrate how the double-differential X-ray scattering cross section can be reconstructed using a novel ghost-imaging algorithm. Corrections for fluorescence from the metal filter need to be applied. The method requires excellent signal levels that can be obtained for molecules with large scattering cross sections, but advances in XFEL technology promise opportunities for a wide range of applications.
items.author: David J. Romano, Benjamin H. Savitzky, Andrés Moreno Carrascosa, Alexander Narkiewicz-Jodko et al.

items.title: Towards direct dynamics simulation of photochemistry without the Born–Oppenheimer approximation
items.summary: The simulation of photochemical reactions requires a quantum mechanical treatment of electronic and nuclear dynamics. Most simulation approaches use the Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation and calculations of nonadiabatic couplings to evolve a wavefunction on a set of BO electronic states. However, the use of BO states presents several challenges, such as discontinuous surfaces, singular terms in the Hamiltonian, and double-valued boundary conditions. We present a direct dynamics approach for molecular vibronic dynamics which does not invoke the BO approximation simply by avoiding diagonalization of the electronic part of the Hamiltonian. By employing a diabatic propagation scheme for the orbitals, we ensure that all electronic terms vary smoothly as a function of nuclear coordinates in a basis of configuration state functions (CSFs). We derive equations of motion for mixed quantum-classical dynamics techniques employing averaged potentials, such that the simulated trajectories evolve on linear combinations of CSF surfaces. We test our approach for lithium hydride and ethylene. In contrast with BO electronic surfaces, we find that all CSF surfaces and couplings are smooth and integrable in the vicinity of conical intersections and weak avoided crossings. Comparisons of the dynamics of photoexcited lithium hydride show that Ehrenfest dynamics reproduce changes in electronic state populations, but lead to over-coherence. Our equations of motion for coupled-trajectory dynamics fail to reduce the over-coherence problem due to the reliance of the derivation on the BO approximation. With further work on the selection of orbitals and the mixed quantum-classical equations of motion, our work shows the potential of a pre-BO wavefunction ansatz for practical nonadiabatic dynamics

items.title: Modular integration of MRSF-TDDFT, NAMD, and QM/MM for excited-state dynamics on the OpenQP platform
items.summary: A balanced and efficient description of excited states is essential for accurately capturing ultrafast relaxation processes. In this context, the recently developed mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) has demonstrated strong performance. However, its broader applicability to realistic systems requires seamless integration with multiscale simulation frameworks. In this work, we present a modular strategy that integrates MRSF-TDDFT with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD) and electrostatic potential fitting (ESPF)-based QM/MM embedding methodologies, in which OpenQP (Open Quantum Platform) serves as a modular electronic-structure backend. To further enhance usability and interoperability, we introduce the Open Simulation Manager (OpenSM), a high-level orchestration framework that unifies QM, QM/MM, and NAMD workflows through a consistent and minimal input interface. The resulting OpenQP-OpenSM provides a flexible and extensible platform for multiscale excited-state simulations, enabling rapid integration of advanced electronic-structure methods and fostering collaborative development.
items.author: Mohsen Mazaherifar, Woojin Park, Simone Bonfrate, Jingbai Li et al.

MRSF-TD-CAM-B3LYP dynamics yield three outcomes: reformation of the initial geometry, formation of a diradical intermediate, and production of the bicyclic photoproduct, reflecting its bifurcating topology and more reliable ground-state description relative to LR-TDDFT. A systematic analysis of exchange-correlation functional dependence within MRSF-TDDFT reveals strong consistency across functionals, with only minor deviations such as the borderline single-path behaviour of BHHLYP and DTCAM-AEE. These findings raise important questions about the reliability, limitations, and future development of black-box excited-state methods for modelling photochemical decay in molecular rotors.

items.title: Perspectives on Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computing: Integer Factoring, Discrete Logarithm Problems
items.summary: We present our perspectives on the current status of, integer factoring and discrete logarithm, algorithms underlying the strength of classical public-key cryptography protocols used in key-exchange, encryption and digital signatures. We present an expository overview of the algebraic, number-theoretic and algorithmic principles behind the canonical, powerful algorithms used in the factoring of large, composite RSA modulii. These cover the two main ideas of group order based methods, and quadratic congruence based methods. We provide the resource estimates for the record breaking factoring based on the general number field sieve. Next we present an overview of the algorithmic theory of quantum computation behind, the polynomial time Shor's quantum algorithm for, period finding in hidden subgroup structure problems. This algorithm has played a key role in advancing post-quantum cryptography, and also in the exciting, contemporary developments in quantum computing, networking, sensing, and materials science as a whole. Latest advances in quantum computing rest on a variety of physics, engineering, algorithms, compilation, hardware, software techniques. There are several tradeoffs based on number of qubits, coherence times, control issues, errors and fault tolerance. In this environment, nuances of mathematical ideas, behind every step of the intricate arithmetical and algebraic computations under quantum models plays a significant role. We provide an overview of some of the recent ideas behind such algorithms. We conclude with a recent deep question on the ultimate feasibility of ultra large-scale, error-free, discrete, quantum computations required typically in cryptanalysis.
items.author: C. E. Veni Madhavan

items.title: Bushbaby Optimization Algorithm: A Nature-inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Approach for Engineering Applications
items.summary: Metaheuristic optimization algorithms are widely used to solve optimization problems; however, designing distinct search mechanisms for exploration and exploitation remains an important research challenge.A new algorithm, Bushbaby Optimization Algorithm (BOA), inspired by the behaviour of the bushbaby, is introduced in this paper.The animal's natural behaviour regarding movement, foraging, and hunting is examined, and two specific behaviours are selected to design the search mechanisms."Nocturnal spatial movement and foraging activity", modeled to facilitate global search, expand search space coverage, and mitigate the risk of premature convergence, forms the basis of the exploration phase.Conversely, the "prey attack and return movement" behaviour is utilized to design the exploitation phase, serving as a mechanism for local search and refinement within promising regions.These behaviours are modeled as algorithmic abstractions within BOA and function as complementary mechanisms to manage the optimization process.The performance of BOA is evaluated using the CEC 2011 test suite, and the results are compared with existing metaheuristic optimization algorithms.The results demonstrate that BOA achieves the top rank in 19 out of 22 problems, representing a success rate of 86.36%.These findings indicate that BOA effectively balances exploration and exploitation and is suitable for a wide range of metaheuristic optimization problems.
items.source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
items.author: Zeinab Montazeri, Mohammad Dehghani, Raed Abu Zitar, Omar Almomani et al.

items.title: Markhor Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm for Solving Optimization Problems
items.summary: This study aims to develop a new nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithm called the Markhor Optimization Algorithm (MOA).The core concept of MOA is derived from the natural behaviors of the Markhor in rugged, rocky, and mountainous terrains.In this approach, predator-aware escape behavior and movement toward more suitable terrain guide exploration and global search, while the security-conscious use of suitable habitats and localized movements form the basis for exploitation and local refinement.These behaviors are translated into mathematical rules-serving as a computational abstraction-to simultaneously manage search space coverage and the gradual improvement of solutions.To evaluate the proposed method's performance, a simulation study is conducted using 23 standard benchmark functions, comprising unimodal test functions (F1-F7), high-dimensional multimodal test functions (F8-F13), and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions (F14-F23).MOA is compared against nine other metaheuristic optimization algorithms across 20 independent runs and 1,000 iterations; performance is assessed using mean, standard deviation (std), rank, and convergence curves.The study's findings demonstrate that MOA delivers stable and highly competitive performance across all three categories of benchmark functions, achieving a rank of 1 for all 23 functions.Consequently, optimization analyses reveal that MOA-by securing the top rank in every benchmark function-acts as the best-performing optimizer with a 100% success rate, demonstrating superior competitiveness against rival algorithms.These results indicate that the design of MOA, leveraging two complementary Markhor behaviors, provides an effective framework for simultaneously managing exploration and exploitation in various opt

items.title: Super Mean Graph Labeling: A Novel Cryptographic Framework Using Five-Star Graphs with Applications in Secure Communications and Epidemic Modeling
items.summary: This paper introduces an innovative cryptographic framework based on super mean labeling of five-star graphs K1,V1 ∪ K1,V2 ∪ K1,V3 ∪ K1,V4 ∪ K1,V5, where V1 ≤ V2 ≤ V3 ≤ V4 ≤ V5. We present a comprehensive mathematical foundation for super mean labeling and develop systematic methodologies for encoding messages through carefully constructed graph structures. Three distinct implementation approaches are demonstrated, incorporating computational techniques through C programming for alphabetical mapping, including subtraction-based and division-based numbering schemes. Each approach is thoroughly illustrated with complete message encoding examples, visual cryptography representations, and detailed security analysis. Beyond cryptographic applications, we extend the framework to epidemic modeling, demonstrating how super mean labeling can represent complex disease transmission dynamics in multi-population systems. The epidemic modeling application includes complete mathematical formulations of multi-population SIR models, transmission matrix encoding through graph labeling, and computational implementations for disease surveillance. Our results establish that five-star graphs with super mean labeling provide optimal balance between encoding capacity and structural complexity, offering robust security through multiple layers of mathematical obfuscation. The integration of graph theory with computational algorithms creates a versatile framework applicable to both secure communications and public health informatics.
items.author: Sudhakar V, Leena S, Anuradha P, DR. Indhumathi R - et al.

items.title: Computational Studies of Triplet State Formation in Zinc Dipyrrin Complexes
items.summary: Zinc dipyrromethene complexes are promising earth-abundant photosensitizers due to their strong visible-light absorption and tunable excited states. To rationally design them for photocatalysis and photodynamic therapy, a molecular-level understanding of triplet-state formation is needed, but details of intersystem crossing remain unclear. To study the effect of π-extension, we synthesized an indole-substituted zinc dipyrrin complex: the dipyrromethane ligand was prepared from indole and mesitaldehyde, oxidized to the dipyrromethene, then coordinated with zinc. DFT and TD-DFT calculations determined ground and excited-state geometries and energies in different solvents, modeled absorption spectra, and visualized charge distributions. The results show how solvent polarity shifts energies of the ground, lowest triplet, and excited singlet states, and influences charge separation in the excited state. These computational findings, coupled with photophysical measurements, will establish a framework for designing zinc dipyrrin complexes with improved triplet state yield.

items.author: Reuben Kwabla Adigbli

items.title: Progression of Mineral Transformer Oils, Including Nanotechnology and Property Evaluation Techniques
items.summary: Mineral transformer oil has long been the industry standard for insulating and cooling power transformers due to its favorable dielectric strength, thermal conductivity, and cost-effectiveness. This paper provides a structured review comprising four main elements: (i) the historical evolution of mineral transformer oils, (ii) standard testing methods for evaluating their dielectric (AC, and Impulse breakdown voltages), thermal, and physicochemical properties, (iii) advancements achieved through the incorporation of nanoparticles such as Al₂O₃, TiO₂, SiO2, Fe3O4@SiO2 Core / Shell, AlN, CQD, MWCNT, Zinc Ferrite, Fe₃O₄, etc.., (iv) a comparative analysis of nanofluids in terms of breakdown voltage, thermal conductivity, and long-term performance. The review highlights that nanofluid formulations offer significant improvements in key operational parameters; however, challenges remain, including nanoparticle sedimentation, optimization of particle concentration, viscosity management, and the risk of accelerated oil degradation. This manuscript concludes by outlining essential steps for future research to establish reliable, standardized, and durable nanofluid-based transformer oils.
items.author: Abd Elrahman S. Tawfic, Mohamed H. Abdo, El‐Sayed M. El‐Refaie, Diaa‐Eldin A. Mansour

items.title: Machine-learning-assisted continuous inverse design of multiring optical fibres for beam shaping
items.summary: This article presents a method for inverse design of multiring optical fibres using machine learning.It proposes fibre configurations expected to yield specified beam-shaping parameters and verifies selected off-grid configurations using independent OptiFiber simulations.The proposed method creates machine-learning surrogate models from numerical simulations performed in OptiFiber.It utilises differential evolution optimisation to predict and optimise the refractive index (RI) profiles of individual fibre layers for given beam parameters.The study reused a dataset comprising 721 valid three-layer optical-fibre configurations previously generated using OptiFiber.For each fibre configuration, the output light beam was simulated, and the full width at half maximum (FWHM), beam flatness and edge steepness were calculated.As the direct prediction of fibre configuration from beam parameters is ambiguous, a surrogate model was employed for subsequent use.The feasibility of using several regression models to create a surrogate model was analysed, including ExtraTrees, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, support vector regression, multi-layer perceptron, ridge regression and the k-nearest neighbours method.Ensemble tree-based models yielded the best predictive performance, with the ExtraTrees model providing the highest overall accuracy and a high degree of agreement between predicted and simulated beam parameters.An ablation study demonstrated that prediction accuracy can be improved by extending the feature set used to train the surrogate model to include descriptors of the differences between the RI values of individual optical fibre layers.The employed inverse design procedure enabled continuous estimation of the optical fibre configuration, reducing the need for exh
items.source: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal
items.author: Marta Dziuba-Kozieł

items.title: Two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems
items.summary: Quantum interactive proof systems can be parallelized to three messages, as shown by Kitaev and Watrous (STOC 2000), perhaps their most striking distinction from classical counterparts. In this work, we establish that any quantum interactive proof system can further be parallelized to two messages, with the verifier sending halves of EPR pairs (``quantum public coins'') and, after the prover's response, using only stoquastic verification. Technically, we strengthen ${\sf QIP}(3) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}$ of Jain, Ji, Upadhyay, and Watrous (JACM, 2011) and fully characterize two-message quantum interactive proof systems by proving \[ {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf StoqAM} = {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf QAM} = {\sf QIP}(2) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}. \] Our main technical contributions show that Close Image to Uniform (CIUniform), which is naturally in the stoquastic version of ${\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf QAM}$, is $\sf PSPACE$-hard via transforming the sum-check protocol of Shamir (JACM, 1992) and Shen (JACM, 1992) into a CIUniform instance consisting of an efficient sampler whose image distribution is exactly uniform for some input distribution when the underlying quantified Boolean formula is true.
items.author: Yupan Liu

items.title: Simple design of adaptive protocols for quantum metrology with limited data
items.summary: Recent sensing experiments have used a Bayesian notion of precision gain to adapt control parameters for fixed measurements. Here, we advocate a simple design principle based on Personick's minimum mean square loss formalism to extend this procedure in order to include measurement optimisation, determining the optimal measurement for each probe and providing a prior-dependent precision gain to optimise the probe itself. This offers a Bayesian counterpart to protocol design based on the Fisher information, with a similar algebraic structure but incorporating the full prior. We apply this principle to adaptive phase estimation with single-mode Gaussian probes, showing that joint optimisation outperforms both adaptive homodyne detection and a fixed-probe strategy optimised for the initial prior, with a maximum reduction of 32% in mean posterior variance relative to homodyne detection. Our results illustrate the potential of simple Bayesian design for quantum metrology with limited data when measurement bases can be controlled.
items.author: Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Jesús Rubio

items.title: Small-world networks yield tunable quantum codes at short circuit depth
items.summary: Monitored random quantum circuits naturally generate quantum error-correcting codes. We generate quantum codes with tunable properties by implementing random Clifford circuits on Watts--Strogatz `small-world' networks and tailor code properties via three knobs: nonlocal graph rewiring, measurement rate, and circuit depth. On fully rewired networks, circuits of logarithmic depth produce codes with a finite rate and an extensive mean contiguous distance with failure probability substantially lower than codes produced from local circuits. These small-world codes form at a circuit depth growing as $\ln n$ compared to polynomial depths required for codes produced from local networks. Rewiring also moves the purification transition to higher measurement rates and changes its critical exponents. Connectivity is thus a knob for designing codes.
items.author: Samuel Bevins, Gregory Bentsen

items.title: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
items.summary: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.
items.author: Bikun Li, Guo Zheng, Liang Jiang

items.title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
items.summary: Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these resources. Local communication can overload one rack's BSMs while others remain idle; reaching those idle resources incurs additional optical loss and retries through switches and quantum frequency converters (QFCs). Programs remain locked into this locality-contention tradeoff as their communication patterns change. We propose Schism, an architecture that lets programs dynamically change which QPUs share each BSM pool. Schism places BSM pools at aggregation switches and QFCs on their core-facing uplinks. Top-of-rack switches establish reconfigurable native-wavelength circuits from QPUs to these pools, forming scale-up domains bounded by the optical loss budget. Reconfiguration reshapes resource sharing across racks without moving QPUs or migrating quantum states. Our key insight is that QPU grouping jointly determines photon-path loss and contention for BSM resources: locality alone cannot identify the best grouping, and a grouping pays off only if its savings outweigh the delay of reconfiguring to it. We develop an optimization framework that combines graph partitioning with resource-constrained completion-time estimates and dynamic programming to select how QPUs share BSM pools and when those groupings reconfigure, between or within circuit phases. Our evaluation using SeQUeNCe with trapped-ion parameters shows that Schism achieves communication speedups of 4.9-7.3x across 11 workloads on 32 QPUs compared to Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6-8.3x compared to SwitchQNet. Schism also outperforms a hypothetical network-wide switch by 1.35-1.38x on t
items.author: Daniel Alexander, Deeksha P Rao, Nilesh Vyas, Vamsi Addanki

items.title: Self-guided estimation of the stabilizer fidelity with single-copy Pauli measurements
items.summary: The stabilizer fidelity quantifies the non-stabilizerness of pure states, but it is hard to estimate because it requires optimizing over $2^{O(n^2)}$ stabilizer states for $n$ qubits. Here, we propose a self-guided estimation protocol for the stabilizer fidelity of an unknown state, pure or mixed, which requires only Pauli measurements on single copies. The protocol moves through the graph of neighboring stabilizer states, obtains the fidelities of a whole stabilizer basis from a single direct fidelity estimation, and reuses previous outcomes, which also provide a restart point that mitigates the barren plateau of a random start. In addition, it certifies the global optimum when the lower confidence bound of the estimated fidelity exceeds $\cos^2(π/8)$. In numerical simulations of up to 14 qubits, the protocol reached the optimum in all runs, with the number of iterations remaining small and increasing only slightly with $n$.
items.author: M. Torres, J. Gidi, L. Pereira

items.title: Floquet spectra and parameter sensitivity of entanglement in the quantum kicked top
items.summary: We investigate the relationship between the Floquet spectrum and the sensitivity of the entanglement landscape to parameter and initial condition change in the quantum kicked top. We focus on the case of four qubits and on locating degeneracies in its Floquet eigenphases using the resultant of its characteristic polynomial $p$ and its derivative $\partial_λp$ and quantitatively map the sensitivity of the entanglement landscape to changes in kicking strength over the sphere of spin coherent initial states. We find that prominent sensitivity maxima coincide with either Floquet eigenphase degeneracies or kick strengths exhibiting short-period quantum revivals, with some points satisfying both conditions. These results establish a connection between the spectral structure of the Floquet operator and entanglement landscape sensitivity, demonstrating the utility of the resultant in studying the dynamics of small-$j$ quantum kicked tops. Since this structure extends to all values of $j$, the central lessons apply completely generally.
items.author: Dyari Jarvis, Peter A. Rose, Arjendu K. Pattanayak

items.title: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
items.summary: Modular exponentiation dominates the logical cost of factoring 2048-bit RSA integers (RSA-2048) with Shor's algorithm. Recent approaches based on approximate residue number systems (RNS) sharply reduce the required logical qubits, yet still demand billions of Toffoli gates. Optimizing these circuits is difficult because shared ancilla qubits and measurement-based uncomputation tightly couple the arithmetic stages, while rare overflows in compressed registers occur too infrequently for random simulation to detect. Here we use large language model (LLM)-driven search to redesign the RNS pipeline across stages and build a deterministic compiler that produces a Pareto frontier of RSA-2048 circuits. We bound rare overflow probabilities analytically and verify the resulting elementary gate sequences across all constituent RNS primes on representative circuits. Relative to Gidney's 2025 baseline under matched adder accounting, our frontier cuts the minimum qubit-Toffoli product by 70.1% and lowers expected factoring Toffolis by up to 78.6% at matched accumulator precision, bringing RSA-2048 factoring below one billion Toffolis for the first time.
items.author: Xiaodi Li, Yuqing Wang, Xue Chen, Yang-Yang Tang et al.

items.title: Protected Charge Readout Scheme Utilizing Nonlinear Resonators
items.summary: Charge detection of nanoscale quantum devices commonly relies on dissipative sensors, where signal absorption causes measurement backaction. Recently, nonlinear resonators showed a near-unity readout signal through an induced frequency shift. We show that this frequency shift protects the sensor, as it detunes the resonator from the measurement signal. The resonator excitation reduces while an enhanced readout signal is maintained. Our results, supported by numerical modeling, show that nonlinear resonators can combine strong readout contrast with reduced measurement-induced backaction.
items.author: Andrea Cicovic, Harald Havir, Pierre Glidic, Samuel Andersson et al.

items.title: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula
items.summary: We construct a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects the critical-line zeros of a regularized zeta function within a continuous spectrum. Starting from the exact Riemann--Siegel integral representation, we define $ζ_{\rm reg}(s)$ by subtracting the contribution of the pole at the origin. The two remaining contour integrals supply the interfering amplitudes. A Dirichlet heat filter suppresses high spatial frequencies, and an arithmetic dressing has a profile generated by prime-power dilations. These transformations map the dilation generator to a self-adjoint, parity--time ($PT$) symmetric Hamiltonian on a physical Hilbert space with a positive metric. Its spectrum is real and continuous. The computed lower critical-line zeros of $ζ_{\rm reg}(s)$ lie close to the corresponding Riemann zeros and exhibit spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.
items.author: Germán Sierra

items.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
items.summary: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including $1/f$ and Lorentzian. These results follow from a general expression, derived here, for the average gate infidelity under arbitrary spatiotemporal noise correlations, valid for generic multiqubit systems and system-environment coupling structures. The infidelity takes the form of a spectral overlap between the noise correlation matrix and a gate-dependent filter function, in which the coherent dynamics of the gate itself shapes the spectral window through which correlated fluctuations enter. The framework converts measured noise correlations into quantitative error budgets and provides a concrete design principle for selecting entangling operations in scalable quantum architectures.
items.author: Xinru Tang, Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Stefano Bosco et al.

items.title: Quantum Approximation and Integration in Sobolev Spaces -- Low Smoothness
items.summary: We study the complexity of approximation and integration in Sobolev spaces in the quantum setting of information-based complexity theory (IBC). Previous results have been obtained under the assumption that the embedding condition holds. Here we drop this assumption and use a quantum version of a previously developed stochastic discretization technique.
