items.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
items.summary: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.
items.author: Xian P. Yang, Christopher T. Parzyck, Martin Cross, Ella Blake et al.

items.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
items.summary: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.
items.author: Anirban Das, Asmi Haldar, Arnab Das

items.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
items.summary: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements. Specifically, we analyse the statistical properties of two distinct state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble (TE) conditioned on the measurement outcomes of the hybrid circuit, and the projected ensemble (PE) generated by further projective measurements of the system at the final temporal boundary. We find that both ensembles undergo non-analytic changes -- ensemble phase transitions -- at the critical point of the measurement-induced purification transition, despite their first moments remaining completely maximally mixed and blind to the transition. For Haar-random circuits, the TE transitions from a trivial identity ensemble to the uniform Haar ensemble, while the PE transitions from the Haar ensemble to a trivial singleton pure state. In Clifford circuits, absence of non-stabiliserness limits the PE to a $1$-design, while the TE forms a $k$-design for $k \leq 3$. We demonstrate that these genuine ensemble transitions offer a clear physical mechanism for the measurement-induced entanglement or purification transitions, illustrating how the capacity to ergodically steer a quantum subsystem shifts from the temporal boundary measurements in the mixed phase to the bulk trajectory measurements in the pure phase.
items.author: Saptarshi Mandal, Sthitadhi Roy

items.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
items.summary: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.
items.author: Omar Bachain, Mohamed Amazioug, Rachid Ahl Laamara

items.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
items.summary: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.
items.author: Bibek Saha, David E. Logan, Sthitadhi Roy

items.title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
items.summary: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.
items.author: Paula I. Villar, Federico Guglielmucci Nazar, Elián Urtubey, Fernando C. Lombardo

items.title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
items.summary: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.
items.author: Zhiyao Yang, Bowen Xiao, Huangjun Zhu

items.title: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
items.summary: Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility. The required number of bases is optimal up to a logarithmic factor in inverse accuracy. In contrast, $d+1$ mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, can minimize mean Fisher anisotropy among families of $d+1$ bases yet have a Fisher floor of at most $1/(d+1)$, showing that optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity.
items.author: Bowen Xiao, Zhiyao Yang, Huangjun Zhu

items.title: Stiffness in Confined Quantum Walks
items.summary: We investigate boundary-induced stiffness in discrete-time quantum walks confined to a finite lattice by unitary reflecting boundaries implemented through coin-flip operations. We define a dimensionless spreading stiffness from the instantaneous variation of the spatial width relative to the asymptotic spreading rate of the corresponding unconfined Hadamard walk and compare localized, Gaussian, and truncated-uniform initial states. The long-time response retains a strong dependence on the initial spatial profile: the localized and truncated-uniform states show an overall increase in stiffness with increasing confinement size, whereas the Gaussian state exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence with a broad maximum at intermediate sizes. The first and second stiffness moments satisfy the expected asymptotic consistency relation in the high-stiffness regime. The normalized Kullback--Leibler divergence reveals a slower spatial reorganization and qualitatively different finite-size trends, showing that dynamical stiffness and spatial homogenization are distinct properties. These results indicate that unitary confinement produces an intrinsically nonstationary regime whose long-time properties emerge from the interplay between boundary reflections, system size, and the spatial structure of the initial state.
items.author: Pablo G. M. Dantas, Rafael Vieira, Edgard P. M. Amorim

items.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
items.summary: Memory effects in open quantum systems do not by themselves imply quantum memory, since non-Markovian dynamics can often be reproduced by classical-memory models. Known criteria certify the presence of quantum memory in the environment by comparing the evolution of the system at two different times. We show that quantum memory can remain hidden from all such pairwise tests and become detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. We derive an analytical three-time witness and use it to certify quantum memory in a minimal qubit example in which every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, thus establishing a strict hierarchy of quantum memory effects. Genuine multi-time quantum memory does not rely on fine-tuned time-dependent Hamiltonians or gate-based evolution. We experimentally demonstrate the hierarchy of quantum memory in a time-continuous realization on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings.
items.author: Konstantin Beyer, Valentin Link, Surihan Sean Borjigin, Qian Cao et al.

items.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
items.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014. With partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation, we obtain 13.5 bit/s over 109 km, and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB of accumulated loss between two cities without a direct fiber link. Benchmarking against finite-key security bounds shows that the implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound, and that replacing detect-and-discard with error correction would increase the finite-key rate by a factor of 4.1-6.6, and yield a positive finite-key rate on the 142.9 km link where the implemented scheme yields none.
items.author: Gilberto Borges, Saeid Salari, Ekta Panwar, Samgeeth Puliyil et al.

items.title: Scalable Pauli propagation through $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear partitioning
items.summary: Pauli propagation simulates quantum circuits and many-body dynamics by evolving observables in the Heisenberg picture as sparse sums of Pauli strings. As Pauli-string operations reduce to bit manipulations, its performance is limited by memory bandwidth and capacity rather than computational throughput. Pooling the memory of many cores and nodes is hindered by the deduplication step after every gate, which can require global synchronization. We avoid this bottleneck by partitioning the strings with an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear hash function, which guarantees that a $k$-qubit channel couples each partition to at most $4^k$ partitions fixed by the gate, decomposing gate application into independent tasks with bounded communication. Benchmarks of our open-source implementation demonstrate efficient parallel scaling within and across compute nodes, enabling simulations with over $10^{11}$ Pauli strings and extending the accessible timescales of quantum many-body dynamics.
items.author: Alev Orfi, Andrew Kille, J. Clayton Peacock, Jack Dunham et al.

items.title: Eight-stage pseudo-symplectic Runge–Kutta methods of order (4, 8)
items.summary: Using simplifying assumptions that are related to the time reversal symmetry, a 1-dimensional family of 8-stage pseudo-symplectic Runge-Kutta methods of order (4, 8), i.e., methods of order 4 that preserve symplectic structure up to order 8, is derived. An example of 7-stage method of order (4, 9) is given.
items.author: М. Г. Степанов

items.title: Guaranteed, locally efficient, and robust a posteriori estimates for nonlinear elliptic problems in iteration-dependent norms: an orthogonal decomposition result based on iterative linearization
items.author: Koondanibha Mitra, Martin Vohralík

items.title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
items.summary: Abstract. The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of existing techniques to compute derivatives of numerical solutions of differential equations. We first discuss the importance of gradients of solutions of differential equations in a variety of scientific domains. Second, we lay out and compare the mathematical foundations of the various approaches. Third, we cover computational considerations and explore the solutions available in modern scientific software. Last but not least, we provide best practices and recommendations for practitioners. We hope that this work accelerates the fusion of scientific models and data and fosters a modern approach to scientific modeling.
items.author: Facundo Sapienza, Jordi Bolíbar, Frank Schäfer, Brian Groenke et al.

items.title: Unified quantification of entanglement and nonstabilizerness in information scrambling and their trade-off relation
items.summary: Entanglement and magic are among the most fundamental properties unique to quantum systems. Each quantity captures a different aspect of non-classical behavior, and each can be regarded as a resource within its own operational setting. However, the interrelation between them has not yet been fully clarified, and whether a more fundamental measure exists remains an open question. Addressing these issues is essential for deepening our understanding of quantumness. In this study, we establish a unified resource theory of information scrambling, consisting of two types: entanglement scrambling and magic scrambling. We introduce a measure that jointly characterizes both types of scrambling. This unified approach reveals a rigorous trade-off relation between entanglement and magic scrambling, as the exact maximum value of the proposed measure can be derived analytically. Furthermore, we quantify the scrambling capability of unitary transformations in terms of their ability to amplify this measure. We also discuss the relevance of our framework to the Pauli propagation method as a practical application. Our work provides insights into the connection between entanglement and magic that extend beyond the context of information scrambling.
items.author: Mao Kaneyasu, Yoshihiko Hasegawa

items.title: Thermodynamic probes of multipartite entanglement in strongly interacting quantum systems
items.summary: Quantifying multipartite entanglement in quantum many-body systems and hybrid quantum computing architectures is a fundamental yet challenging task. In recent years, thermodynamic quantities such as the maximum extractable work from an isolated system (the ergotropy) have allowed for entanglement measures that are operationally more accessible. However, these measures can be restrictive when applied to systems governed by Hamiltonians with strong collective or interparticle interactions. Motivated by advances in quantum simulators, we propose a framework that circumvents these restrictions by evaluating global and local ergotropy either through controlled quenching of interactions or by measuring suitable local observables only. We show that this formalism allows us to correctly estimate genuine multipartite entanglement in both stationary and time-evolved states of systems with strong interactions, including parametrized quantum states simulated on a quantum circuit with varying circuit depth and noise. We demonstrate its applicability to realistic physical models, namely, the Tavis-Cummings model, the three-level Dicke model, and the transverse-field Ising model, highlighting its potential as a versatile tool for characterizing entanglement in near-term quantum simulators.
items.author: Harsh Sharma, Sampriti Saha, A. S. Majumdar, Manik Banik et al.

items.title: Discrete shift and polarization from response to symmetry defects in interacting topological phases
items.summary: We extend the previous study of extracting crystalline symmetry-protected topological invariants to the correlated regime. We construct the interacting Hofstadter model defined on square lattice with the rotation and translation symmetry defects: disclination and dislocation. The model realizes Chern insulator and the charge density wave state as one tunes interactions. Employing the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method, we calculate the excess charge around the defects and find that the topological invariants remain quantized in both phases, with the topological quantity extracted to great precision. This study paves the way for utilizing matrix product state, and potentially other quantum many-body computation methods, to efficiently study crystalline symmetry defects on 2D interacting lattice systems.
items.author: Lu Zhang, Min Long, Yuxuan Zhang, Zi Yang Meng et al.

items.title: The quantum agreement theorem
items.summary: Intersubjective consistency asks when different observers of a physical system, reasoning from a shared theory, will agree on their probability assessments. Classical probability theory provides a benchmark in the form of the Agreement Theorem [R. J. Aumann, Ann. Stat. 4 , 1236–1239 (1976)]. We study the quantum mechanics (QM) analog to the classical Agreement Theorem in a finite-dimensional tripartite setting in which two observers obtain information via local projective measurements. We represent their mutual awareness by common certainty, which is formally an infinite hierarchy of certainty operators concerning the probability of an event of interest. We first prove that if the observers’ measurements commute with one another and with the property of interest, common certainty forces their probability assessments to coincide, thereby recovering a QM analog to the classical Agreement Theorem. We then construct a one-parameter family of qutrit–qubit–qubit models in which one observer’s measurement does not commute with the property and common certainty of disagreement occurs—a distinctively QM phenomenon. The mechanism is coherence between branches distinguished by one but not the other observer’s measurement. When measurement outcomes are stored in a classical register, the resulting dephasing removes this coherence and restores agreement. Finally, we prove that QM does not permit the extreme 0 - 1 configuration in which Alice is certain of a property and is also certain that Bob is certain of its negation. These results aim to turn debate in QM about observer-dependent facts into precise mathematical conditions for when intersubjective agreement or disagreement in QM can be sustained.
items.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
items.author: María García Díaz, Adam M. Brandenburger, Giannicola Scarpa

items.title: Observation of an anomaly in the statistics of Kibble-Zurek defects
items.summary: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism quantifies defect formation during adiabatic passage across a continuous phase transition, providing key insights into universality in quantum many-body systems. We explore counting statistics of defects in adiabatic passage experiments on long 1D Rydberg atom chains. The experiments reveal an anomaly in the defect number distribution at long ramp times, challenging the hypothesis of defect formation through independent domain mergers. Numerical simulations confirm the anomaly and suggest its link to non-critical coarsening dynamics, which we suppress in prepare-and-hold experiments. Our results highlight the ability of quantum simulators to uncover unexpected correlated quantum phenomena.
items.author: J. Balewski, Alexey Khudorozhkov, Siva Darbha, Omar A. Ashour et al.

items.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance
items.summary: Abstract The evolution of quantum states can be described by quantum channels. The task of estimating an unknown quantum channel, known as process tomography, is a central problem in quantum information theory. A long-standing open question is how many uses of an unknown channel are required to learn it to a precision quantified by the standard metric for distinguishing quantum processes, known as the diamond distance. Here we address this by establishing the query complexity of channel tomography with optimal dependence on the dimensions of the input and output spaces and the channel’s Kraus rank at any fixed constant accuracy in diamond distance. We design an algorithm that establishes an upper bound and prove a matching lower bound for learning a channel to the given accuracy. Our algorithm follows the strategy of performing optimal tomography on the Choi-state representation of the process, and we show that channel tomography can be reduced to the well-studied problem of pure-state tomography. As channels subsume states, unitaries and measurements as special cases, our protocol provides a unified framework for tomography of these tasks.

items.title: Tuning long-range interactions in Sr Rydberg atoms: the effect of series perturbations
items.summary: Abstract We investigate the effect of series perturbation on the second-order dipole-dipole interactions between strontium atoms in the 5 s n s ( 1 S 0 ) and 5 s n p ( 1 P 1 ) Rydberg states as a means of engineering long-range interactions between atoms. The series perturbation in these atoms enables modifying the strength and the sign of the interaction by varying the principal quantum number n of the Rydberg electron. We utilize experimentally available data to estimate the importance of perturber states, and find that the van der Waals interaction between two strontium atoms in the 5 s n p ( 1 P 1 ) states shows strong peaks that deviate from the anticipated hydrogenic n 11 scaling. We identify this to be the result of the perturbation of 5 s n d ( 1 D 2 ) intermediate states by the 4 d 2 ( 1 D 2 ) and 4 d n ′ s ( 1 D 2 ) states in the n < 20 range. This demonstrates that divalent atoms offer a unique advantage for generating substantially stronger or weaker inter-atomic interactions than those that can be achieved using alkali metal atoms. items.source: Journal of Physics B Atomic Molecular and Optical Physics
items.author: Türker Topçu, Andrei Derevianko

items.title: Measurement of Parity-Dependent Energy-Phase Relations in a Potential Artificial Kitaev Chain Utilizing a Transmon Qubit
items.summary: Abstract Artificial Kitaev chains have emerged as a promising platform for realizing topological quantum computing. Once the chains are formed and Majorana zero modes are braided/fused, reading out the parity of the chains is essential for verifying the non-Abelian property of Majorana zero modes. Here, we demonstrate a transmon-based microwave probe for a four-site quantum dot–superconductor chain based on a Ge/Si nanowire. One end of the chain is incorporated into a superconducting transmon circuit, enabling spectroscopic identification of the chain’s singlet/doublet ground state and thereby inference of its total Fermion parity. We also demonstrate that, for multiple-dot chains, there are two types of 0−π transitions between different charging states: the parity-flip 0−π transition and the parity-preserved 0−π transition. Furthermore, we demonstrate electrostatic tunability of the interdot coupling. This phase-sensitive microwave platform provides a tool for studying complex hybrid superconducting quantum dot systems and for future extended artificial Kitaev chains.
items.author: Enna Zhuo, Xiaozhou Yang, Yuyang Huang, Zhaozheng Lyu et al.

items.title: Nonlinear cooling and control of a mechanical quantum harmonic oscillator
items.summary: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)–component Schrödinger’s cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.
items.author: Matteo Simoni, Ivan Rojkov, M. Mazzanti, Wojciech Adamczyk et al.

items.title: The Entangling of Supernova Feedback Impacts with Coarsening Simulation Resolution
items.summary: It is often understood that supernova (SN) feedback in galaxies is responsible for regulating star formation (SF) and generating gaseous outflows. However, a detailed look at the small-scale effects of SNe on the interstellar medium (ISM) in simulations shows that the macroscopic processes of SF suppression and outflow generation proceed in distinct channels. We demonstrate this finding in two independent simulations of isolated dwarf galaxies with very high (m_gas ~ Msun) numerical resolution, LYRA and RIGEL. Our findings suggest that the macroscopic effect of a given SN on the galaxy is best predicted by its local density. Outflows are primarily linked to SNe in diffuse regions expanding to their cooling radii on large (~kpc) scales, while dense SF regions are disrupted in a localized (~pc) manner. However, these separate feedback channels are only distinguishable at very high resolutions capable of following mass scales ^2 . When averaging on coarser scales, ISM densities are greatly mis-estimated, and variations between different SF and SNe-affected regions are severely washed out. It therefore cannot be self-consistently determined, from coarse-resolution information alone , (1) whether a SN tends to contribute to outflows or direct SF suppression, and (2) the rate of SF in a given region. In particular, commonly used parameters in coarse-resolution (subgrid) models, such as the SN cooling radius and SF density threshold, may require more detailed treatments informed by high-resolution studies.
items.author: Eric Zhang, Laura V. Sales, Thales A. Gutcke, Yunwei Deng et al.

items.title: Differentiable quantum-trajectory simulation of Lindblad dynamics for QGP transport-coefficient inference
items.summary: Abstract We study parameter estimation for the transport coefficients of the quark-gluon plasma by differentiating open-quantum-system-based Monte Carlo simulations of quarkonium suppression. The underlying simulator requires solving a Lindblad equation in a large Hilbert space, which makes parameter estimation computationally expensive. We approach the problem using gradient-based optimization. Specifically, we apply the score-function gradient estimator to differentiate through discrete jump sampling in the Monte Carlo wave-function algorithm used to solve the Lindblad equation. The resulting stochastic gradient estimator exhibits sufficiently low variance and can still be estimated in an embarrassingly parallel manner, enabling efficient scaling of the simulations. We implement this gradient estimator in the existing open-source quarkonium suppression code QTraj. To demonstrate its utility for parameter estimation, we infer the two transport coefficients κ and γ using gradient-based optimization on synthetic nuclear modification factor data.
items.author: Lukas Heinrich, Tom Magorsch

items.title: Principles of use of tensile J-curve materials in antagonistic arrangements
items.summary: Natural ligaments are soft connective tissues that provide high stretchability for dexterous flexibility but switch to high stiffness to protect the musculoskeletal system from excessive deformation. These two functions cannot be independently tuned in conventional engineering materials with linear or hyperelasticity. Biological materials achieve this tailored behavior through a highly nonlinear tensile response characterized by a J-shaped curve, featuring an extended “toe region” of low force up to intermediate strains followed by an inflection, called the “heel region” which marks the onset of nonlinear stiffening. Here, we aim to study the characteristics of J-curves to establish principles for their use in robotic mechanisms. We define and measure the J-curve features responsible for protectiveness and mobility, describe the effective stiffness and the level of nonlinearity as a function of pre-stretch, and elucidate how the J-curve decouples flexibility from damage protection. Experimental measurements reveal the performance advantages of twisted and coiled elastomeric J-curve materials in engineered antagonistic arrangements and highlight their unique design space compared with linear elastic systems. Furthermore, we present a conceptual analysis of exploiting J-curve materials in energy-efficient running as an outlook toward their use in bioinspired robots.
items.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
items.author: Liuyang Cheng, Wonsik Eom, Qiong Wang, Hyeongkeun Kim et al.

items.title: Gravitational wave signatures from periodic orbits around a Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson black hole
items.summary: Abstract In this paper, we investigate periodic bound orbits and gravitational wave (GW) emission in the Schwarzschild–Bertotti–Robinson (Schwarzschild–BR) spacetime—an exact electrovacuum solution describing a static black hole (BH) immersed in a uniform magnetic field. We explore how the background magnetic field qualitatively alters the BH's gravitational dynamics, affecting timelike geodesics such as the marginally bound orbit (MBO) and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We then analyze periodic bound orbits using the ratio of the azimuthal and radial frequencies, which characterizes the orbits by their azimuthal and radial motions. Based on the numerical kludge method, we further compute the gravitational waveforms emitted from periodic orbits around a supermassive Schwarzschild–BR BH. We show that the background magnetic field changes the orbital frequencies, resonance conditions, zoom–whirl structures, and the resulting waveforms. Finally, we compute the frequency spectra in the mHz band and estimate the signal-to-noise ratio for LISA, Taiji, and TianQin. Our results show how a magnetic field that is part of the spacetime geometry affects periodic orbits and their gravitational-wave signals.
items.author: Tursunali Xamidov, Sanjar Shaymatov, Qiang Wu, Tao Zhu

items.title: Modeling the inner electric double layer using short-range machine learning potentials: A critical assessment
items.summary: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical interfaces typically require large system sizes and long simulation times to obtain reliable thermodynamic properties. In this context, machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) allow for computationally efficient sampling compared to density functional theory-based molecular dynamics simulations. Although conventional short-range MLIPs are recognized as inadequate for modeling the (potentially nanometer-wide) diffuse layer, they may still be capable of describing the inner electric double layer that is relevant for electrochemical reactions. Here, we evaluate the performance of common (short-ranged) MLIP architectures [the deep potential DP, the (graph) atomic cluster expansion-based models GRACE and MACE, and the pre-trained eSEN-OC25] for charged Au/electrolyte interfaces. In the evaluation, we focus on the effect of message passing and on the potentially adverse effect of data interference when training for a broad range of surface charges. Our results suggest that both local and message-passing models are able to reliably learn the interfacial structure when training on a single charge state. However, when trained on datasets that span multiple charge states, the MLIPs tested yield inconsistent predictions of interfacial water orientation and ion distributions. This behavior can be traced to the MLIPs being "blind" to the actual surface charge. Message-passing models show somewhat greater robustness to mixed-charge training data, likely due to their larger receptive field, but are still prone to artifacts and errors in the description of the interfacial structure. Overall, our results provide practical guidance on the expected accuracy and cross-charge-state transferability of short-ranged MLIPs for the description of
items.author: Lucas B. T. de Kam, Jiaxin Zhu, Ankit Mathanker, Katharina Doblhoff-Dier et al.

items.title: Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
items.summary: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.
items.author: Adarsh P. Raghuram, Francesca M. Blondell, Jonathan M. Mortlock, Benjamin Maddox et al.

items.title: Real-Space Visualization of Site-Selective Co 3 d States in the Ising Magnet Ca 3 Co 2 O 6
items.summary: High-spin Co 3+ ions can retain a finite orbital contribution and exhibit pronounced magnetic anisotropy, providing model systems for Ising magnetism. However, direct real-space observations of their orbital states remain limited. Here, we visualize the site-dependent Co 3d electronic states in the Ising-chain magnet Ca 3 Co 2 O 6 , which contains crystallographically inequivalent high-spin and low-spin Co 3+ sites, using synchrotron X-ray diffraction and valence electron density (VED) analysis based on core differential Fourier synthesis. The octahedral Co site exhibits a VED distribution consistent with a low-spin state, whereas the trigonal-prismatic Co site shows pronounced anisotropy that cannot be reproduced by crystal electric field (CEF) effects alone. A wavefunction analysis incorporating CEF effects, spin–orbit coupling, and ligand-mediated Co 3d–O 2p–Co 4p hybridization reproduces the observed VED anisotropy. These results establish a site-selective real-space picture of the Co electronic states and demonstrate the capability of VED analysis to probe local orbital states and orbital hybridization in quantum materials.
items.source: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan
items.author: K. Gautam, Shunsuke Kitou, Yuiga Nakamura, Norimasa Sasabe et al.

items.title: Space-bounded quantum state testing via space-efficient quantum singular value transformation
items.summary: Abstract Driven by exploring the power of quantum computation with a limited number of qubits, we present a novel complete characterization for space-bounded quantum computation, which encompasses settings with one-sided error (unitary ) and two-sided error ( ), approached from a quantum (mixed) state testing perspective: The first family of natural complete problems for unitary $$\text {\textsf {coRQL}} $$ coRQL , namely space-bounded quantum state certification for trace distance and Hilbert–Schmidt distance; A new family of (arguably simpler) natural complete problems for , namely space-bounded quantum state testing for trace distance, Hilbert–Schmidt distance, and (von Neumann) entropy difference. In the space-bounded quantum state testing problem, we consider two logarithmic-qubit quantum circuits (devices) denoted as $$Q_0$$ Q 0 and $$Q_1$$ Q 1 , which prepare quantum states $$\rho _0$$ ρ 0 and $$\rho _1$$ ρ 1 , respectively, with access to their “source code”. Our goal is to decide whether $$\rho _0$$ ρ 0 is $$\epsilon _1$$ ϵ 1 -close to or $$\epsilon _2$$ ϵ 2 -far from $$\rho _1$$ ρ 1 with respect to a specified distance-like measure. Interestingly, unlike time-bounded state testing problems, which exhibit computational hardness depending on the chosen distance-like measure (either -complete or -complete), our results reveal that the space-bounded state testing problems, considering all three measures, are computationally as easy as preparing quantum states. Our results primarily build upon a space-efficient variant of the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) introduced by Gilyén, Su, Low, and Wiebe (STOC 2019), which is of independent interest. Our technique provides a unified approach for designing space-bounded quantum algorithms. Specifically, we sho
items.author: François Le Gall, Yupan Liu, Qisheng Wang

items.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
items.summary: Electric flux strings underpin confinement in gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, their evolution involves competing processes of charge motion, pair creation, and transverse deformation. Accessing these dynamics beyond perturbative limits challenges classical approaches, as entanglement growth restricts the times accessible to tensor-network simulations. Here we use quantum simulation to investigate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction, spanning strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. Using 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, we evolve initially localized strings with static or dynamical endpoint charges. Spatially resolved measurements reveal rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation in the string interior near the pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields. String-path occupations further probe transverse rearrangements between configurations connected by plaquette operations. Retaining separate matter and gauge degrees of freedom makes local Gauss-law constraints directly accessible for error detection. Combining these constraints with ancilla checks and noise rescaling, we measure dynamics in circuits containing up to 15 second-order Trotter steps. Our results establish quantum simulation as a practical approach to exploring nonperturbative string dynamics in two spatial dimensions, with gauge redundancy serving as an experimental resource.
items.author: Sanziana Stelea, Anthony Gandon, Francesco Tacchino, Jad C. Halimeh et al.

items.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm
items.summary: Visible and near-ultraviolet light underpins applications from biophotonics to quantum computing, which demand fast control of optical amplitude and phase. Integrated photonics offers scalable control, yet most visible-wavelength platforms lack gigahertz-scale modulation. We demonstrate a thin-film lithium niobate platform at 493 nm integrating grating couplers, beamsplitters, ring resonators, and modulators. Segmented traveling-wave modulators achieve a half-wave voltage--length product of 450 mV$\cdot$cm, $>$20 dB extinction, and bandwidth beyond 50 GHz. Ring resonators show $2.9 \pm 0.2$ dB/cm propagation loss and quantify the platform's photorefractive response. This enables agile visible beam delivery for trapped-ion systems, although photorefraction and substrate uniformity remain key challenges to scaling.
items.author: Nicholas Achuthan, Letícia Magalhães, Xudong Li, Hugo Voncken et al.

items.title: Finite-Key Readiness and Authentication-Key Replenishment in QKD-Assisted UAV Edge Computing
items.summary: A service that needs fresh quantum keys must wait for key release, and may be denied it, before protected computation starts. We quantify this cost for a trusted stationary UAV serving two ground gateways, each obtaining its keys from one finite-key decoy-state BB84 attempt with parameters fixed in advance. A count-level Monte Carlo model, reproduced by a semi-analytic model, links key acceptance to protected upload, computation, and download, including failed attempts and hover energy. At 26~dB effective optical loss, with authentication hashing at its proxy-benchmarked, near-zero cost, fresh keys raise the 95th-percentile completion time of both tasks from 10.37 to 28.65~s; hover energy grows in proportion. The scalar rate models evaluated here miss the deadline limit on the block size. The pulse budget lies in a window bounded below by authentication-key replenishment and above by the deadline; for a fixed source, channel, and acceptance model, the authentication debit shifts the floor, whereas hashing cost does not. At a 35-s deadline the largest tested loss with a non-empty window is 27~dB at 1\% misalignment and 22~dB at 2\%; at 3\% no tested setting has one. Conditional on the assumed acquisition probability, the selected configurations meet this deadline with simultaneous lower confidence bounds of 96.9--97.3\% on held-out trials, at 26~dB and at 18--20~dB with 2\% misalignment. A high-cost stress reference that charges hashing in full narrows the window and lowers these loss limits to 26 and 20~dB at the reference processing capacity. A small rise in error rate or loss pushes the deadline probability well below its target and drains authentication keys, while the protocol's security parameter is unchanged.
items.author: Dang H. Le, Ban Q. Tran, Susan Mengel

items.title: Structure of correlations for the single-$j$ model using quantum information theory
items.summary: We say that a system undergoes a quantum phase transition when the mean-field ground state of a given Hamiltonian spontaneously breaks its symmetries depending on the Hamiltonian parameters. It is a widely accepted view that this phenomenon enables the mean-field state to absorb the maximum amount of correlations without losing its mean-field structure. However, it is still uncertain how those correlations are incorporated within the mean-field state and how the correlation structure changes when we get closer to the exact ground state by restoring the symmetries. In this work, we answer these questions by studying the single-$j$ model, which is a realistic fermionic nuclear model with abelian and non-abelian broken symmetries. We find that both types of symmetries have very different effects for the correlations within the mean-field state. This makes unclear the concept of the symmetry breaking process as a mechanism to absorb the maximum amount of correlations. Moreover, the symmetry restoration redistributes existing `fake' correlations between paired orbitals to more complex subsystems.
items.author: Javier Faba, Vicente Martín, Luis Robledo

items.title: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling
items.summary: Thermal amplification enables sensitive control of heat currents, providing a basis for heat management and thermal signal processing in quantum devices. For a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, we recover the absence of thermal amplification when system-reservoir interactions permit only single-quantum exchange. A controlled weak-nonlinearity expansion, supported by numerical stationary solutions, shows that two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification and predicts its onset. When two-quantum exchange dominates at the emitter and collector, varying the base temperature redistributes populations between even and odd oscillator sectors. This changes the emitter and collector heat currents far more than the base current, enabling large thermal amplification. We propose a realization using a longitudinally coupled auxiliary two-level system and bath spectral filtering, specifying conditions for its elimination to yield the required oscillator dynamics. These results establish nonlinear system-reservoir coupling as a resource for controlling heat flow and enabling thermal amplification.
items.author: Laiba Hayat, M. Tahir Naseem

items.title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors. We analyze the linear-depth multiplexer and the noise-resilient bucket-brigade architectures, adapting the latter to a native superconducting gate set and refining its fidelity analysis using the fully decomposed gate schedule. For a representative bucket-brigade QRAM query with a $12$-qubit address register we obtain a query fidelity of $0.969$. The query consumes $3.51\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{J}$ of dynamic energy, corresponding to an average dynamic power of $4.38\,\mathrm{W}$ and a peak of $64.4\,\mathrm{W}$. Our optimization shows that, at fixed target fidelity, the operating point and attenuation profile can change the average power by a factor of two or more.
items.author: Joao F. Doriguello, Alessandro Luongo, Harshit Verma

items.title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes
items.summary: The theory of turbo iterative decoding was brought into the quantum coding framework through the development of quantum serial turbo codes and quantum block turbo codes. In this paper, we present a theory for multidimensional quantum block turbo codes, a turbo decoding technique for multi layer product codes. We describe its algorithm and simulate the performance for the 3D case on a depolarizing channel.
items.author: Khaled Jebari, Luiz Anet Neto, Ramesh Pyndiah, Jean-Louis de Bougrenet de la Tocnaye

items.title: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers
items.summary: Tavis--Cummings lattices couple cavities containing several emitters and host polaritonic many-body dynamics whose real-time correlations are costly to compute classically in two dimensions, especially when unequal emitter relaxation or dephasing rates break permutation symmetry. We analyze logical resources for fault-tolerant closed- and open-system simulation of an atom-resolved lattice with $L$ cavities, $N$ emitters per cavity, and photon cutoff $n\_{\max}$, including target observable estimation. Building on ladder-operator block encoding, we construct circuits for photon hopping and local light--matter exchange and combine them to encode the lattice Hamiltonian. By updating source and destination photon occupations in place, the hopping circuit eliminates the auxiliary $L\lceil\log_2(n\_{\max}+1)\rceil$-qubit photon register used by two-register implementations. Across three uniform-coefficient examples with $16$ to $256$ cavities, the controlled walk uses $4.75$--$8.11%$ fewer Toffoli gates than the paired two-register implementation under matched shared preparation, precision, control, and workspace conventions. For closed systems, we implement real-time evolution with generalized quantum signal processing and bound the cost of estimating retarded cavity spectral functions. For open systems with photon loss, emitter relaxation, and dephasing, we use a sampled first-order dilation and bound the runs and timesteps needed to estimate transient photon statistics such as $g^{(2)}(0)$. With state-preparation and measurement costs explicit, these estimates provide a reference for assessing fault-tolerant light--matter lattice simulation costs.
items.author: Soumya Sarkar, Rakshit Gharat, Nam Nguyen, Gavin Brennen

items.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
items.summary: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK. A 400-ns reset pulse yields residual excited-state populations of $0.29\%$ and $0.67\%$ for qubits initialized in $|g\rangle$ and $|e\rangle$, respectively. We further demonstrate efficient leakage removal from the $|f\rangle$ state, reducing its residual population to $0.51\%$. These results establish a simple, reproducible, and easy-to-integrate approach to dissipation engineering in superconducting quantum processors.
items.author: Feiyu Li, Yang Liu, Zhen Yang, Zhenxing Liu et al.

items.title: Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results
items.summary: We implement reference renewal to reconsider retained physical quantum-service results under a prespecified protocol. Twelve transitions retained six results each; ten completed renewal, eight met the prespecified endpoint, and five succeeded using retained results alone. The exact one-sided p=0.0546875 does not establish the recovery hypothesis. Incomplete references, binding failures and sequential waits expose operational limits. Offline reconstruction recovers decisions from preserved counts. Retrospective binding-plus-oracle checking accepts all 60 usable-transition results without renewal. With the exact oracle also supplying calibration scores, the study does not demonstrate incremental numerical-correctness utility of renewal.
items.author: Roberto Fernández-Barrios, Iker Pastor-López, Amaia Pikatza-Huerga, Pablo García Bringas

items.title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
items.summary: Many image classification tasks have labels that are unchanged by rotations and reflections. Equivariant quantum neural networks incorporate such symmetries by design, but the specific benefit of symmetry is difficult to isolate. Equivariant quantum circuits are usually compared with architectures that also differ in gates, structure or size. Here, we investigate the role of invariance in a controlled setting, classifying images whose labels are invariant under the dihedral group $D_4$. We compare four eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and number of trainable parameters, and equivalent dynamical Lie algebras, and benchmark invariant implementations against non-invariant ones in terms of generalization error, robustness to shortcut learning and resilience to a realistic noise model. On four binary tasks, including MNIST and two scientific data sets of galaxies and red blood cells, the invariant models trained on a few tens of images show better generalization than non-invariant ones. Invariance also makes the models immune to orientation shortcuts: when trained with a class-dependent corner watermark, the non-invariant models learn the watermark and often drop to chance level when it is moved. We show that the gain in accuracy of invariant models persists also under a realistic noise model.
items.author: Giuseppe D'Ambruoso, Giovanni Gramegna, Domenico Pomarico, Giuseppe Magnifico et al.

items.title: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits
items.summary: We develop a control strategy for fluxonium qubits based on picosecond single-flux-quantum (SFQ) pulses generated by Josephson digital circuits. A major challenge is that SFQ protocols originally designed for transmon control become inefficient for low-frequency fluxonium. In this regime, the asymmetry of flux and charge couplings leads either to excessive leakage or excessively long gate times. We show that this limitation can be overcome by two complementary protocols. The first protocol employs high-frequency SFQ pulse packets applied through the flux channel, offering a simple, analytically transparent, and robust approach for high-fidelity single-qubit control. The second protocol combines phase-shifted flux and charge pulse sequences to enhance the resonant drive and reduce the gate duration. Multilevel simulations demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities above $99.99\%$; the simpler protocol remains robust under moderate variations of qubit parameters and flux bias, while the combined protocol preserves high fidelity while substantially accelerating the gate. These results establish SFQ-based cryogenic control as a realistic route to fast, accurate, and scalable manipulation of fluxonium qubits.
items.author: M. V. Bastrakova, D. S. Pashin, V. A. Vozhakov, N. V. Klenov et al.

items.title: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm with cat qubits
items.summary: Abstract The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)–a prominent candidate for near-term quantum computing applications–is tailored to find approximate solutions to combinatorial optimization problems using shallow quantum circuits. In this work, we investigate implementations of QAOA based on cat qubits, where the logical states $$|0\rangle$$ and $$|1\rangle$$ are represented by coherent states of opposite amplitudes, $$|\alpha \rangle$$ and $$|-\alpha \rangle$$ . Within this encoding, the primary source of noise–photon loss–induces a bias toward Z -type errors. We focus specifically on an imlementation employing Kerr resonators. By numerically simulating the gate sequences required for QAOA on these nonlinear resonators, we analyze performance on Max-Cut problems and benchmark it against conventional qubits realized as ideal two-level systems subject to single-photon loss. Our findings indicate that the use of cat qubits leads to improved approximation ratios for random Max-Cut instances compared to standard qubit encodings.
items.author: Pontus Vikstål, Laura García-Álvarez, Shruti Puri, Giulia Ferrini

items.title: Learning State Preparation Circuits for Quantum Phases of Matter
items.summary: Many-body ground state preparation is an important subroutine used in the simulation of physical systems. In this paper, we introduce a flexible and efficient framework for obtaining a state preparation circuit for a large class of many-body ground states. We introduce polynomial-time classical algorithms that take reduced density matrices over O ( 1 ) -sized balls as inputs, and output a circuit that prepares the global state. We introduce algorithms applicable to (i) short-range entangled states (e.g., states prepared by shallow quantum circuits in any number of dimensions, and more generally, invertible states) and (ii) long-range entangled ground states (e.g., the toric code on a disk). Both algorithms can provably find a circuit whose depth is asymptotically optimal. Our approach uses a variant of the quantum Markov chain condition that remains robust against constant-depth circuits. The robustness of this condition makes our method applicable to a large class of states, whilst ensuring a classically tractable optimization landscape.
items.author: Hyun-Soo Kim, Isaac H. Kim, Daniel Ranard

items.title: Time Series Analysis in Frequency Domain: A Survey of Open Challenges, Opportunities and Benchmarks
items.summary: Frequency-domain analysis has emerged as a powerful paradigm for time series analysis, offering unique advantages over traditional time-domain approaches while introducing new theoretical and practical challenges. This survey provides a comprehensive examination of spectral methods from classical Fourier analysis to modern neural operators, systematically summarizing three open challenges in current research: (1) causal structure preservation during spectral transformations, (2) uncertainty quantification in learned frequency representations, and (3) topology-aware analysis for non-Euclidean data structures. Through rigorous reviewing of over 100 studies, we develop a unified taxonomy that bridges conventional spectral techniques with cutting-edge machine learning approaches, while establishing standardized benchmarks for performance evaluation. Our work identifies key knowledge gaps in the field, particularly in geometric deep learning and quantum-enhanced spectral analysis. The survey offers practitioners a systematic framework for method selection and implementation, while charting promising directions for future research in this rapidly evolving domain.
items.author: Qianru Zhang, Yuting Sun, Honggang Wen, Peng Yang et al.

items.title: Statistical benchmarking of optimization methods for a variational quantum eigensolver under quantum noise
items.summary: This work investigates the performance of numerical optimization algorithms applied to the State-Averaged Orbital-Optimized Variational Quantum Eigensolver for the H2 molecule under various quantum noise conditions. The goal is to assess the stability, accuracy, and computational efficiency of commonly used gradient-based, gradient-free, and global optimization strategies within the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum regime. We systematically compare six representative optimizers, BFGS, SLSQP, Nelder-Mead, Powell, COBYLA, and iSOMA, under ideal, stochastic, and decoherence noise models, including phase damping, depolarizing, and thermal relaxation channels. Each optimizer was tested over multiple noise intensities and measurement settings to characterize convergence behavior and sensitivity to noise-induced landscape distortions. The results show that BFGS consistently achieves the most accurate energies with minimal evaluations, maintaining robustness even under moderate decoherence. COBYLA performs well for low-cost approximations, while SLSQP exhibits instability in noisy regimes. Global approaches such as iSOMA show potential but are computationally expensive. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting suitable optimizers in variational quantum simulations, highlighting the importance of noise-aware optimization strategies for reliable and efficient quantum chemistry computations on current hardware.
items.author: Silvie Illésová, Tomáš Bezděk, Vojtĕch Novák, Bruno Senjean et al.

items.title: On the complexity of the succinct state local Hamiltonian problem
items.summary: Abstract We study the computational complexity of the LOCAL HAMILTONIAN problem under the promise that its ground state, or a low-energy state, is succinctly represented. We show, for qubit Hamiltonians, that the SUCCINCT LOW-ENERGY STATE 2-LOCAL HAMILTONIAN problem, is (promise) MA -hard and the SUCCINCT GROUND STATE 3-LOCAL HAMILTONIAN problem is (promise) MA -complete. Our approach combines a systematic characterisation of succinct quantum states, defined through arithmetic over specific number fields, with a refined complexity-theoretic reduction that lowers the locality of Feynman–Kitaev circuit-Hamiltonians from 6 to 2, without increasing particle dimension. Since the 1-local case is solvable in P , these results narrow the locality-parameterised complexity transition and extend the scope of known MA -complete problem instances. Our results further clarify how succinctness behaves under circuit-based constructions, and progress towards a better understanding of the boundary between efficiently describable and efficiently verifiable quantum systems.
items.author: Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin

items.title: Generalized Fermat’s principle and Snell’s law for cone structures and applications
items.summary: Fermat’s principle is fully generalized to the case where a smooth interface separates two cone structures—Lorentz-Finsler lightcones—representing wave propagation in a potentially inhomogeneous, anisotropic, time-dependent and discontinuous medium. The interface, wave source and receiver are assumed to be a hypersurface, a submanifold and a curve in the spacetime, respectively, of any causal character. For a trajectory to fulfill Fermat’s principle—i.e., to be a critical point of the arrival time functional—its direction must change at the interface, obeying a precise condition that generalizes Snell’s law of refraction when the wave crosses the interface, or the law of reflection when it remains in a single medium. Both laws are analyzed in detail to establish the conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of refracted and reflected trajectories, and to determine whether they actually minimize the arrival time. Applications to Zermelo’s navigation problem and the determination of geodesics in discretized spacetimes are also emphasized.
items.author: Miguel Ángel Javaloyes, Steen Markvorsen, Enrique Pendás-Recondo, Miguel Sánchez

items.title: Kondo cloud conductance in cavity-coupled quantum dots with asymmetric barriers
items.summary: The Kondo effect emerges when a localized spin is screened by conduction electrons, giving rise to a strongly-correlated many-body ground state. In this work, we investigate this phenomenon in a GaAs/AlGaAs quantum dot, focusing on the spatial extension of the Kondo screening cloud in the electron reservoirs. To probe its properties, the dot is coupled to an electronic Fabry-Pérot interferometer, enabling controlled modulation of the density of states at the Fermi level. The observation of Kondo temperature oscillations indicates a Kondo screening length comparable to the cavity size. Furthermore, we explore how the coupling asymmetry with the two reservoirs affects both the amplitude and the phase of the conductance oscillations, revealing a subtle interplay between coherent transport and Kondo effect.
items.author: Diego Fossion, V. Champain, Sambit Mohapatra, A. Cavanna et al.

items.title: Hofstadter-Herman visualization as a diagnostic tool for systematic effects in electromagnetic form factor extractions
items.summary: The internal charge and magnetization distributions of the proton are characterized by the electromagnetic form factors G E and G M . They are extracted from elastic electron-proton cross sections measured at fixed momentum transfer over a range of beam energies and scattering angles via Rosenbluth separation. Conventionally, form factor values are obtained by plotting reduced cross sections against the virtual photon polarization parameter ϵ and then extracting the slope and intercept of the best-fit lines. An alternative visualization method, proposed by Hofstadter and Herman in 1960, plots form factors directly instead. The values of G E 2 and G M 2 are immediately visible from the intersection region of the curves and their uncertainty bands. In this work, we apply Hofstadter-Herman visualization to classic 1994 SLAC elastic scattering data. The 1994 data include a ∼ 4% downward normalization adjustment applied to the 1.6 GeV/ c spectrometer measurements. Overlaying modern global fit extractions on Hofstadter-Herman plots, we show that intersection regions obtained without including this adjustment sit closer to the global fit values. Such tensions are not readily visible in conventional plots. Our results motivate adopting this visualization method as a routine diagnostic cross-check at the Electron–Ion Collider and elsewhere to flag normalization shifts and related adjustments before they enter global fits.
items.author: Tyler Williams, Jennifer Rittenhouse West, Douglas W. Higinbotham, F. Benmokhtar

items.title: Geometric characterization of non-Gaussian entanglement for finite stellar rank states
items.summary: We introduce a general framework for the analysis of non-Gaussian entanglement in bosonic states of finite stellar rank. The central result is the full characterization of their entanglement structure through the atomic decomposition of their stellar polynomial and its associated structural graph, whose connected components determine the mode-intrinsic entanglement content of the state and all partitions compatible with passive separability. An essential ingredient in this construction is the concept of essential variables, which identify the minimal number of effective modes involved in a core state, in direct correspondence with the symplectic rank. This reduction provides the foundation for decomposing stellar polynomials into atomic factors and for revealing the underlying entanglement structure. Building on this, we derive complete separability criteria for two-mode states, expressed through hyperplane decompositions of zero sets, and for stellar-rank-2 states across an arbitrary number of modes. Applications to several example states illustrate how the method isolates genuinely non-Gaussian resources and quantifies preparation complexity.
items.author: Carlos E. Lopetegui, Massimo Frigerio, Mattia Walschaers

items.title: Quantum neural networks for wind power prediction: a benchmark against classical machine learning models
items.summary: Abstract Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is an emerging field at the intersection of quantum computing and machine learning that aims to enhance classical learning methods by leveraging principles such as superposition and entanglement. However, skepticism remains regarding its practical advantages, particularly due to the limitations of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. This study addresses these concerns through a systematic evaluation of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), quantum-inspired counterparts of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). We construct and analyze 12 distinct QNN configurations by combining two quantum feature maps with six entanglement strategies for ansatz design. Experiments conducted on a wind energy dataset show that QNNs can achieve competitive or superior performance compared to classical baseline models, with the best-performing configuration (QNN-3) reaching an R 2 score of up to 0.94 when forecasting wind power output using four input features. In addition, we provide a detailed analysis of simulation time across different configurations, highlighting trade-offs between model complexity and computational cost. These findings demonstrate the potential of QNNs as viable models for predictive tasks and contribute to the ongoing evaluation of QML in real-world applications.
items.author: Batuhan Hangun, Onder Eyecioglu, Mehar Ali, Oguz Altun et al.

items.title: Towards the simulation of higher-order quantum resources: a general type-theoretic approach
items.author: Samuel B. Steakley, Elia Zanoni, Carlo Maria Scandolo

items.title: Generation of spatiotemporal optical coil with controllable transverse intensity chirality
items.summary: Chirality is a fundamental asymmetry in nature. In optics, control of chirality is evolving from spatial properties like polarization to the temporal chirality of local fields. Conventional approaches, however, encode chirality in abstract degrees of freedom such as phase or polarization, limiting direct and efficient coupling with matter on ultrafast timescales. We introduce and experimentally demonstrate a paradigm of intensity-driven optical chirality, where handedness is physically inscribed into the trajectory of spatiotemporal energy flow. Through the engineered non-collinear collision of Spatiotemporal Optical Vortices, the spatiotemporal optical coil is generated. The coil's chirality manifests as a physical torsion of its volumetric energy flow, a property distinct from chirality hidden in phase or polarization. By employing femtosecond tomography and phase-resolved reconstruction, we map the complete three-dimensional spatiotemporal intensity field, directly observing the evolution of singularity lines. This approach reveals programmable scaling relations between the coil's topology and interaction geometry, extending the concept of chirality to the energy-flow level. The introduced volumetric chiral density directly correlates with the optical forces and torques exerted on chiral particles, providing an intensity-manifested degree of freedom for topological photonics and enabling novel schemes for ultrafast chiral-selective excitation and high-dimensional information encoding.
items.author: Dana JiaShaner, Xingyuan Zhang, Huiming Wang, Zhirong Tao et al.

items.title: Four-loop quark-to-quark splitting function in QCD
items.summary: The scale evolution of parton distributions is governed by splitting functions. We compute the four-loop pure-singlet contribution to the quark-to-quark splitting function in perturbative QCD. Together with the known non-singlet contribution, our result completes the quark-to-quark splitting function at this order. We confirm previous partial results and obtain, for the first time, a fully analytic expression valid for all momentum fractions. We examine its behavior at small momentum fractions and provide precise numerical representations suitable for parton evolution.
items.author: Thomas Gehrmann, Andreas von Manteuffel, Vasily Sotnikov, Tong-Zhi Yang

items.title: Dephasing-Induced Melting of Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
items.summary: Long-range spectral order can be probed using spectral form factors, where it manifests itself as sharp Bragg peaks at integer multiples of the Heisenberg time in nearly crystalline spectra. We examine how energy dephasing in open systems affects this spectral order and how to control it. We find that Bragg peaks fade algebraically with revival order and dephasing strength, $K_{\rm Bragg}(p)\propto(γp)^{-1/2}$, within an extensive intermediate regime, and persist up to the lifetime of nearest-neighbor coherences despite an extreme decoherence rate. Our results establish the spectral form factor as a probe of spectral order in open quantum systems and identify temporal correlations in spectral fluctuations as a means of controlling it.
items.author: Preethi Gopalakrishnan, Adolfo del Campo

items.title: Chiral waveguide model for error-correctable quantum computation
items.summary: We develop a first-principles framework connecting microscopic waveguide scattering to quantum error correction and algorithmic performance. For polarization-encoded single photons interacting with an ensemble of two-level atoms in a chiral waveguide, we derive an effective polarization quantum channel by tracing out the frequency degree of freedom. Using this channel as the physical noise model for a rotated planar code, we observe threshold behavior as the number of atoms $N$ and the atom-waveguide coupling strength $Γ$ are varied. An asymptotic analysis of the microscopic scattering model explains the threshold scaling with $NΓ/σ$, where $σ$ is the photon spectral bandwidth. For identical, lossless atoms with symmetric real coupling and a photon spectrum centered at resonance, the effective noise is strongly biased toward $X$ errors. We then incorporate the resulting logical errors into quantum phase estimation and demonstrate that the noise bias can guide circuit design. In particular, a Hadamard-basis implementation reduces sensitivity to the dominant error, improving algorithmic performance.
items.author: Zixiang Hong

items.title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
items.summary: Estimates of when photonic devices outgrow classical simulation are hard to compare: even for single-photon boson sampling, quoted thresholds range from 50 to 98 photons, as they rest on different tasks and assumptions. We propose as a common unit the time a classical computer needs to draw one sample from the device's exact output distribution, up to floating-point rounding. Only exactness applies equally to every kind of light, since the cost of approximate sampling depends on the accuracy required. The simulability frontier is the device size at which our fastest exact sampler produces one sample per second on a fixed machine; this device size increases with better hardware and algorithms. As the time per sample grows exponentially with the number of detected photons, doubling the machine speed moves the frontier by about one photon, whereas a better algorithm changes the growth rate. We measure the frontier with photonic-engines, an open-source GPU library of exact samplers for single photons, entangled photons from quantum emitters, vacuum-single-photon superpositions and squeezed light. Each sampler is validated against a simulator sharing no code with it. On one NVIDIA H100 GPU, with Haar-random interferometers, twice as many modes as photonic inputs and photon-number-resolving detectors, the frontier lies at 38.3 single photons and at 31.0 entangled photons from one emitter. For squeezed light, a timing model fitted to measurements places it at 41.5 squeezed photonic inputs of mean photon number 0.5. For our samplers, coherence alone makes simulation harder: sources that emit a photon with probability one half reach 64.2 when vacuum and photon are mixed incoherently, as for lossy single photons, but only 50.0 when they are in coherent superposition. Feed-forward
items.author: Jean Senellart, Benjamin Stott, Stephen Wein, Esperanza Cuenca Gomez et al.
