items.title: Quantum Error Correction in Nearly Critical Toric Codes
items.summary: We investigate quantum error correction protocols for topological codes deformed away from their stabilizer limits, particularly as they are pushed towards quantum phase transitions into trivial phases. Our focus is primarily on quantum information stored within the ground-state manifold of the transverse-field toric code (TFTC), subjected to independent bit-flip and phase-flip decoherence. Although the transverse field induces strong quantum fluctuations of $m$ anyons in the ground states, we show that projective measurements of the "bare" toric code stabilizers can nevertheless be used to construct an efficient decoding algorithm which exhibits a finite threshold to both types of decoherence, even when the transverse field is tuned infinitesimally close to the quantum critical point. Our construction of the optimal postmeasurement decoders---that is, the optimal decoders assuming that the stabilizers are first measured---crucially relies on the stoquastic nature of the TFTC Hamiltonian, which affords a description of its ground states in terms of a classical lattice gauge theory. Using stoquasticity, we first prove that stabilizer measurements act unitarily on the undecohered TFTC ground states to excellent approximation, and that the optimal postmeasurement decoder can be efficiently implemented via Monte Carlo simulation of a constrained lattice gauge theory. We then construct the optimal postmeasurement decoder for the TFTC states under bit-flip and phase-flip decoherence, where we numerically demonstrate a finite threshold close to the quantum critical point. We provide theoretical evidence (without a rigorous proof) that stabilizer measurements constitute an optimal decoding strategy in this setting. For phase-flip decoherence, we further prove that the optimal p
items.author: Zack Weinstein, Samuel J. Garratt

items.title: Quantum Pointwise Dimension (QUPID): An algorithm for identifying classical chaos in quantum dynamics
items.summary: The Pointwise Dimension is a diagnostic that reveals the effective dimensionality of classical trajectories in a $2N$-dimensional phase space. The essence of this diagnostic is to find a scaling according to which density changes with radius $r$ around a point of interest in phase space. Particularly, regular trajectories are confined to an $N$-dimensional invariant torus, while chaotic trajectories explore a $(2N-1)$-dimensional energy surface. In classical mechanics, this trajectory density can be found by counting recurrences to within the sphere of radius $r$. In quantum mechanics, probability density is intrinsic, making the Pointwise Dimension compelling, but surprisingly this has not been studied in the quantum regime. In this work, we implement the Pointwise Dimension in the quantum regime using the Husimi representation of the quantum wavepacket. This implementation entails a long-time average of the time-dependent Husimi representation to obtain a stationary phase space density, and a radial spatial integration of this density over a sphere of radius $r$. The classical-quantum correspondence is excellent for both autonomous and non-autonomous systems, adding a new diagnostic to the study of quantum chaos. Finally, we explore the possibility, both classically and quantum mechanically, of obtaining the Pointwise Dimension from a time correlation function.
items.author: Jonathan Berkheim, David J. Tannor

items.title: Breaking the quantum barriers for Graph Collision
items.summary: In the graph collision problem, the task is to decide whether a known graph on $n$ vertices contains an edge with both endpoints marked, given query access to the input bits specifying the marked vertices. We first refute the conjectured $Ω(n^{2/3})$ query lower bound with a bounded error quantum algorithm using $\widetilde O(n^{92/139})$ queries. We then refine this approach to obtain a $\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ query algorithm. We also obtain a $\widetilde O((nq)^{11/17})$ query bound for all (partial) Boolean output functions with positive certificate complexity at most 2 and alphabet size $q$, contrasting a known $Ω(n^{2/3})$ lower bound for such problems with large alphabet sizes. We complement these algorithms with an $Ω(\sqrt{n\log n})$ quantum query lower bound for graph collision, exceeding the $O(\sqrt n)$ certificate complexity barrier for the positive adversary method.
items.author: Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, Shiva Kintali, François Le Gall et al.

items.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
items.summary: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference, with about 98k parameters outside the embedding, the model reaches $76.98 \pm 0.17$% test accuracy, level with a softmax transformer of the same size ($76.62 \pm 0.36$%). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 45% of test pairs, out of the 53% any single deletion can change, against 32% for the softmax model explained the same way and 40% by its attention x gradient. Attention can look more like the words annotators highlighted, yet accounts for the answer less well: deleting the word it ranks first changes the Born Transformer's answer in 32% of pairs. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics and to qubits, and a coherent attention layer becomes one circuit equal to the model (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps by Hadamard tests, the device gave the model's answers on two short test pairs and kept or changed them under deletion as the model does; the evidence itself did not yet survive the device, and we work out the shots and calibration that measuring it on hardware would need.
items.author: Teerawat Tongloy, Jiraporn Pongsopa, Rangsan Jomtarak

items.title: Interpretable Quantum Photonic Generative Models
items.summary: We propose a physical generative model for learning correlated multivariate data based on homodyne detection of photonic continuous-variable (CV) circuits. We use an $N$-mode photonic circuit in which two-mode squeezing provides correlations, local phase shifts tune the strength and sign of these correlations, and an adjustable interferometer redistributes them across modes. We train the circuit by matching its Pearson correlation matrix to the one obtained from data. We apply affine post-processing to adjust the marginals independently while keeping the relations intact. We test the model on the multivariate distribution of standardized log returns of financial assets, showing that the photonic model can represent rich correlation structures. We reproduce empirical correlations with residuals below $10^{-4}$ for five variables and recover the correct correlation signs for $94\% \pm 1\%$ of 190 correlation pairs at twenty variables, with $86\%$ of the residuals below $0.1$. As a separate technical contribution, we develop an approach for simulating Kerr gates with small nonlinearity via a Hubbard-Stratonovich expansion, making them suitable for CV-based simulators. Our results establish CV photonic circuits as a platform for interpretable generative learning, suitable for representing and fast sampling of distributions across different application domains.
items.author: Dat Chi Le, Oleksandr Kyriienko

items.title: Simple proof of conditions requiring maximal entanglement for local state verification and discrimination
items.summary: For deterministic state verification by separable measurements, the Schmidt rank of an entangled resource must be at least that of the state being verified [N. Yu, R. Duan, and M. Ying, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 60, 2069 (2014)], and if the two are equal, the resource must be maximally entangled [S. Akibue, J. Miyazaki, and H. Osaka, Lett. Math. Phys. 116, 110 (2026)]. The latter was derived from a general theorem proved using algebraic geometry. In this paper, we give a simple, self-contained proof of both statements using only linear algebra. We then use these results to show that among pure entangled resources of local dimension at most $d$, a maximally entangled state of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$ is necessary and sufficient for perfect local discrimination of a generic orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$, however weakly entangled. The same holds for local implementation of a generic orthogonal measurement.
items.author: Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay

items.title: Quantum Advantage has Few Complexity Implications
items.summary: We consider the complexity implications of proofs of quantumness and (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation. We show that both of these objects can coexist with the easiness of nondeterministic computation. That is, we give evidence that proofs of quantumness can exist when $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP}$ and that (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation can exist when $\mathsf{BQP} = \mathsf{QCMA}$. In particular, we give a classical oracle relative to which (1) $\mathsf{P}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{NP}^\mathcal{O}$ (2) $\mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{PSPACE}^\mathcal{O}$ (3) Proofs of quantumness exist. In particular, there exists a language in $\mathsf{IP}^\mathcal{O} \subseteq \mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O}$ which is hard on average against $\mathsf{P}^\mathcal{O}/poly$. We give a unitary oracle such that (1) $\mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{QCMA}^\mathcal{O}$ (2) Quantum verifier oblivious state preparation exists. These oracle separations directly imply a number of related consequences. For example, our first result implies that proofs of quantumness cannot be used to construct classical or quantum cryptography with a relativizing proof. Our second result implies that quantum computation/classical communication oblivious transfer cannot be used to construct post-quantum one-way functions with a relativizing proof.
items.author: Eli Goldin, Alex Lombardi, Tomoyuki Morimae

items.title: Universal dynamics of quantum phase transitions with fractional long-range interactions
items.summary: The complete statistical characterization of defects generated in a quantum phase transition has mostly been studied in exactly solvable models, and remains little explored in nonintegrable systems such as long-range interacting spin chains. We characterize the full defect counting statistics in a nonintegrable long-range spin chain, the fractional Ising model, by time-dependent variational-principle simulations within the matrix-product-state and matrix-product-operator formalism. Fractional interactions capture emergent multiscale correlations and long-range effects in nature, governed by the order of the underlying fractional derivative. Such couplings can be approximated on existing quantum simulation platforms, where the full defect statistics can be measured. The defect number cumulants follow power laws in the driving time, with exponents that vary continuously with the fractional order. At low fractional order, deep in the long-range regime, the mean defect number decays more slowly than predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), while at intermediate order the KZM holds with the numerically extracted many-body critical exponents. At large fractional order, the exactly solvable free-fermion limit of the model becomes progressively more accurate towards the short-range limit. We derive exact bounds on the kink-number cumulants and on the kink-kink correlations, implying an exact Gaussian limiting distribution for large system sizes. In the many-body simulations, however, kinks are more correlated, consistent with the confinement of domain walls, and these bounds are violated in the long-range regime, also in the bulk of the chain. Nevertheless, the kink distribution still approaches a Gaussian for large defect numbers, with proportionality partially broken be
items.author: Andraás Grabarits, Lincoln D. Carr, Adolfo del Campo

items.title: Effective Hamiltonians and non-Hermitian physics
items.summary: Every realistic quantum system is coupled to an environment. Including the environment restores a closed, Hermitian description, but at the cost of an intractably large Hilbert space. The Feshbach--Löwdin projection eliminates the unwanted degrees of freedom exactly, yielding an effective Hamiltonian $H_{\rm eff}$ on the relevant subspace alone---which \new{generically becomes non-Hermitian when the eliminated subspace contains an energetically accessible continuum and outgoing boundary conditions are imposed}. We illustrate this through a minimal model: a particle in a box with a delta barrier at its center. Direct elimination of one half-well reduces all information about the discarded sector to a single \new{boundary parameter} $β$; the same result is then rederived via the Green's function and Dyson equation, offering a pedagogical illustration of how boundary data enter the Green's-function formalism and relating $β$ to a self-energy term. Whether $β$ is real or complex determines whether $H_{\rm eff}$ is Hermitian or not, and the full range of behavior---from Hermitian dynamics through finite-width resonances to the counterintuitive quantum Zeno effect---follows from this single parameter.
items.author: Ugo Lair, David Guéry-Odelin

items.title: DynaMite: Dynamic Measurement Scheduling To Accelerate Fault-Tolerant Quantum Programs
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computers run millions of logical cycles to perform quantum error correction (QEC). As logical operations span entire logical cycles, the logical cycle time (LCT) dictates program runtime. Qubit measurements, critical to extract parity information for QEC, are the slowest operations and account for 43-86% of LCT. Measurement latencies impact fidelity: fast measurements lower our ability to correctly classify quantum states, whereas slow measurements increase the likelihood of decoherence. Hardware providers thus calibrate measurement latencies that maximize readout fidelity per qubit and use them to schedule all measurements during program execution. However, calibrated latencies are sub-optimal for logical performance because logical cycles span multiple QEC rounds, during which data qubits are not measured. This increases LCT and logical error rates (LERs) due to decoherence at the logical level. We propose DynaMite, a lightweight real-time measurement latency selection policy built on two key insights. First, logical cycles must use a measurement latency that is fast enough to reduce both LCT and LER for the QEC code, instead of the calibrated latency that only maximizes readout fidelity. Second, not all logical cycles are equal; many do not fully utilize the error budget of the QEC code, i.e., the number of failed parity checks it can tolerate without compromising LER. These cycles could use even faster measurements but do not, because latencies are chosen statically, whereas error information is only available at runtime. DynaMite exploits the fact that a logical cycle comprises multiple QEC rounds and selects the fastest latency for an upcoming round based on the error budget left and rounds remaining. Our evaluations show that DynaMite redu
items.author: Dongwhee Kim, Suhas Vittal, Poulami Das

items.title: Efficient simulations of spectra and transport for multiorbital quantum impurities
items.summary: Quantum impurity calculations become challenging when multiple correlated orbitals are treated explicitly, particularly in nonequilibrium steady states. We introduce Coupled-Cluster Coupled Lindblad (C$^3$L), a deterministic approach that combines the recently developed coupled-Lindblad compact bath representation with coupled-cluster theory to compute steady states and Green's functions directly in imaginary and real frequency. C$^3$L has favorable polynomial computational complexity and avoids the sign problem of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). In a real-time multiorbital benchmark, it agrees closely with state-of-the-art QMC while reducing computational cost by four to five orders of magnitude, with a further 10--100-fold speedup on a GPU. Beyond the practical reach of established real-time QMC solvers, four-orbital nonequilibrium impurities with general interactions and biased reservoirs become accessible with C$^3$L. We obtain resonance-resolved transport signatures relevant to scanning tunneling microscopy experiments on molecular junctions.
items.author: Hao-En Li, Zhen Huang, Lin Lin

items.title: Quantum Query Lower Bounds from Classical Moment Matching
items.summary: We prove a quantum analogue of the classical moment matching method, a popular framework used to prove lower bounds in property testing. For two random variables $X_0$ and $X_1$ whose moments match up to the first $r-1$ moments, the classical moment matching method says that no classical algorithm can reliably distinguish between input instances of length $N$ constructed from $X_0$ and $X_1$, respectively, unless it performs at least $Ω(N^{1-1/r})$ queries. While this method has been widely explored since its inception in the seminal work of Raskhodnikova, Ron, Shpilka, and Smith (STOC 2007) to prove lower bounds for symmetric properties, it has remained an open question whether a quantum analogue of it could be proved. We prove two variants of this quantum moment matching method, which are incomparable. Our first quantum query lower bound scales as $Ω(N^{1/2-1/(2r)})$, while our second moment matching theorem yields a sharper lower bound of $Ω(N^{1/2-1/(2(2^r-1))})$, albeit for smaller parameter ranges. Our results combine a new continuous hybrid argument with the polynomial method. The continuous hybrid argument compares two hard input distributions generated from i.i.d. samples by continuously varying both distributions, keeping them identically distributed at every intermediate stage. It reduces the comparison to the effect of changing the distribution of a single sample. The polynomial method then cancels the terms determined by the matched moments. We apply these moment matching theorems to prove new optimal lower bounds on $k$-distinctness, $k$-star-freeness, planarity and outerplanarity testing, as well as to improve prior lower bounds on image size testing and $K$-junta testing by logarithmic factors. A key advantage of our framework is its simplicity: it reduc
items.author: Chandrima Kayal, Frédéric Magniez, Sayantan Sen, Dániel Szabó

items.title: Irreversibility of quantum field theory in de Sitter: The C, F and A theorems
items.summary: We prove the C C , F F and A A irreversibility theorems in de Sitter spacetime for quantum field theories that are obtained as renormalization group flows from ultraviolet conformal fixed points. The proof is based on strong subadditivity of the entanglement entropy, de Sitter invariance, and the Markov property of conformal field theory.
items.author: Nicolás Abate, Gonzalo Torroba

items.title: Tensor network representations for intrinsically mixed-state topological orders
items.summary: Tensor networks are an efficient platform for representing topological states of matter as well as computing both physical observables and information-theoretic quantities. We present a general protocol to construct tensor network representations for intrinsically mixed-state topological phases. Such phases naturally emerge in noisy long-range entangled quantum systems, and exhibit nontrivial topological phenomena without pure-state counterparts. The method exploits the isomorphism between anyon decoherence in the physical Hilbert space and anyon condensation in the corresponding Choi space. The protocol is applicable to a broad class of systems arising from decoherence of pure-state topological phases, where the incoherent noise creates excitations in the Choi space that have trivial monodromy with all excitations. Representative examples at renormalization group fixed points include $m^a e^b$ decoherence in the $\Z_N$ toric code, decohered non-Abelian quantum double of $S_3$ as well as pure $Z$/$X$ decoherence of arbitrary CSS codes. Another notable example is that of the mixed-state chiral semion, whose tensor network representation has no pure-state analogue. We then generalize the formalism beyond RG fixed points and, as an example, examine the decoherence transition in a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ toric code channel that suffers from sign problem when mapped to a statistical mechanical model. Together, these results establish tensor networks as a natural platform for analyzing noisy intrinsically mixed-state topological matter.
items.author: Bader H. Aldossari, Sergey Blinov, Zhu-Xi Luo

items.title: Modelling optimal implementation of an arbitrary N-qubit quantum gate within the generalized Bloch vectors formalism
items.author: Elena R. Loubenets, Sergey Kuznetsov

items.title: Orbital magnetization from parallel transport of Bloch states
items.summary: Abstract Quantum geometric formulations of linear and nonlinear responses can be constructed from a single building block in the form of a gauge-invariant interband transition operator. Here, we identify a second building block for quantum geometry: a band-resolved adiabatic connection operator that captures the noncommutativity between Bloch projectors and their momentum derivatives. The band-resolved adiabatic connection operator, first introduced in the theory of adiabatic driving, serves as a generalized angular momentum within the state manifold of single bands, and we employ it to reformulate expressions for the band-resolved orbital magnetic moment. This form provides a complementary geometric interpretation alongside the multiband separation between energetic- and quantum-state properties by the two-state Berry curvature. Our formalism allows us to present formulas valid for both nondegenerate and degenerate bands, thereby removing the limitations of the common Bloch-state formula. We illustrate our theory by calculating a large orbital magnetization emerging without spin-orbit coupling in a spin-compensated, noncoplanar anomalous Hall magnet with degenerate bands.
items.author: Johannes Mitscherling, Jan Priessnitz, Libor Šmejkal

items.title: Novel qubits in hybrid semiconductor–superconductor nanostructures
items.summary: Hybrid semiconductor-superconductor qubits have recently emerged as a promising alternative to traditional platforms, combining material advantages with device-level tunability. A defining feature is their gate-tunable Josephson coupling, enabling superconducting qubit architectures with full electric-field control and offering a path toward scalable, low-crosstalk quantum processors. This approach seeks to merge benefits of superconducting and semiconductor qubits, for instance by encoding quantum information in the spin of a quasiparticle occupying an Andreev bound state, thus combining long coherence times with fast, flexible control. Progress has accelerated through bottom-up engineering of Andreev states in coupled quantum dot arrays, leading to architectures such as minimal Kitaev chains hosting Majorana zero modes. In parallel, Hamiltonian-protected designs aim to enhance resilience against local noise and decoherence by exploiting superconducting phase dynamics and discrete charge or flux degrees of freedom. This article reviews recent theoretical and experimental advances in hybrid qubits, providing an overview of physical mechanisms, device implementations, and emerging architectures, with emphasis on their potential for (topologically) protected quantum information processing. While many designs remain at proof-of-concept stage, rapid progress suggests practical demonstrations may soon be achievable.
items.author: Marta Pita‐Vidal, Rubén Seoane Souto, Srijit Goswami, Christian Kraglund Andersen et al.

items.title: Study of C P violation in Λ b 0 → N * M decays with the final-state rescattering mechanism
items.summary: In this work, we investigate the charmless non-leptonic two-body $Λ_b$ decays within the framework of final-state rescattering mechanism. In contrast to the Cutkosky cutting method, we compute both the absorptive and dispersive parts of the hadronic rescattering triangle diagrams. Based on the established formalism, we analyze the $Λ_b \to N^*(1535,1520)M$ decay processes with $M =K_S, K^*_0(700)$, $f_0(500,980), ρ(770), \bar{K}^{*0}$, $ϕ$, and predict various physical observables, such as their branching ratios, direct and partial-wave $CP$ asymmetries, as well as decay asymmetry parameters. These two-body decay processes are expected to contribute primarily to the subsequent four-body decay channels, such as $Λ_b^0 \to p\,π^-\,π^+\,π^-$, whose $CP$ asymmetry measurements will be accessible at the LHCb experiment.
items.author: Hao Shang, Tian-Liang Feng, Jing Gao, Qin Qin et al.

items.title: Efficient quantum convolutional neural networks for image classification: overcoming hardware constraints
items.summary: Abstract While classical convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have revolutionized image classification, the emergence of quantum CNNs (QCNNs) presents new opportunities with high-dimensional transformations that are infeasible for classical CNNs. However, their implementation on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remains challenging due to hardware limitations. In our research, we address this challenge by introducing fragment encoding that significantly reduces the input dimensionality. We show that accuracy improves as the number of qubits increases from 1 to 4 to 16, providing evidence of favorable scaling. Motivated by this, we developed a primitive QCNN architecture with $$\varvec{49}$$ qubits which is sufficient to directly process $$\varvec{28 \times 28}$$ pixel MNIST images, eliminating the need for classical dimensionality reduction pre-processing. Additionally, we propose an automated framework based on expressibility, entanglement, and complexity characteristics to identify the building blocks of QCNNs, parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs). Our approach demonstrates advantages in convergence speed with a similar parameter count compared to both LM-QCNNs and classical CNNs. We validated our experiments on IBM’s Heron r2 quantum processor, achieving $$\varvec{96.08\%}$$ accuracy with approximately $$\varvec{70\%}$$ faster convergence relative to classical CNNs under identical training conditions. Our results show that simple image-classification tasks can be realized on real quantum hardware today.
items.author: Peter Röseler, Oliver Schaudt, Helmut Berg, Christian Bauckhage et al.

items.title: Boosting Single‐Molecule Fluorescence Enhancement With Nanoaperture‐Nanoantenna Hybrid Systems
items.summary: ABSTRACT Boosting the sensitivity of single‐molecule fluorescence detection (SMFD), an unique tool in bio‐ and medical sciences, can be enabled by optical nanoantennas exhibiting hotspots to enhance light‐matter interactions. However, precisely delivering molecules into hotspots with nanoscale sizes remains a great challenge for conventional nanoantennas with open interfaces. Here, we integrate carefully designed PMMA‐substrated titanium nanoapertures with nanoantennas, and experimentally demonstrate that the hybrid systems can enhance the signal‐to‐background ratio of SMFD by up to 16 times compared to bare nanoantennas, although requiring higher molecular concentrations to achieve comparable detection efficiency. We design and fabricate a series of hybrid systems, and experimentally show that the unique “nanoaperture‐confined hotspot” configuration formed in our systems can significantly enhance the probability of molecules accessing the hotspot region and shield low‐enhancement events outside the hotspot region, thereby enhancing the single‐molecular fluorescence signals with narrower enhancement distributions and diminished background signals. Our strategy can find many applications in bio‐ and medical sciences, such as single‐molecule sequencing, surface‐enhanced optical sensing, and so on.
items.author: Ting Chen, Zheyuan Zhu, Boyi Liu, Qiong He et al.

items.title: Coupling light with matter for identifying dominant subnetworks
items.summary: We introduce DOMINO, a light-matter computing platform that exploits the full complex amplitude of coupled condensate networks to solve maximum-weight clique problems and reveal hidden indirect correlations in large graphs. By embedding network structure directly into a gain-controlled polaritonic (or photonic) oscillator array, DOMINO performs analog optimization, directly solving the maximum-weight clique problem via the gain-controlled minimisation, through a physically enforced global-intensity constraint, allowing the system to converge rapidly to dominant subnetworks while simultaneously extracting phase, encoded co- and counter-regulation patterns. This gain-based mechanism unlocks capabilities inaccessible to conventional Ising-type simulators: all degrees of freedom (amplitude and phase) participate in the computation, dramatically expanding the class of problems that can be efficiently encoded. Our approach is inherently ultrafast, energy-efficient, and naturally robust to noise, requiring no digital post-processing. Applied to real gene-gene coexpression data, DOMINO reliably identifies biologically meaningful transcription-regulator modules and exposes latent regulatory relationships. Because the method applies generically to any weighted network, it establishes a scalable physical route to solving high-value graph-analytic tasks across biology, finance, social systems, and engineered networks.
items.author: Airat Kamaletdinov, Natalia G. Berloff

items.title: Tensor-network approach to quantum optical state evolution beyond the Fock basis
items.summary: Understanding the quantum evolution of light in nonlinear media is central to the development of next-generation quantum technologies. Yet, modeling these processes remains computationally demanding, as the required resources grow rapidly with photon number and phase-space resolution. Here, we introduce a tensor-network approach that efficiently captures the dynamics of nonlinear optical systems in a continuous-variable representation. Using the matrix product state (MPS) formalism, both quantum states and operators are encoded in a highly compressed form, enabling direct numerical integration of the Schrödinger equation. We demonstrate the method by simulating degenerate spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) and show that it accurately reproduces established theoretical benchmarks—energy conservation, pump depletion, and quadrature squeezing—even in regimes where conventional Fock-basis simulations become infeasible. For high-intensity pump fields (\alpha=100) ( α = 100 ) , the MPS representation achieves compression ratios below 3×10^{-4} 3 × 10 − 4 while preserving physical fidelity. This framework opens a scalable route to modeling multimode quantum light and nonlinear optical phenomena beyond the reach of traditional methods.
items.author: Nikolay Kapridov, Egor Tiunov, Dmitry Chermoshentsev

items.title: Enhanced quantum sensing mediated by a cavity in open systems
items.summary: Abstract We simulate the dynamics of systems with N = 1-20 qubits coupled to a cavity in order to assess their potential for quantum metrology of a parameter in the open systems limit. The qubits and the cavity are both allowed to have losses and the system is studied under various coupling strength regimes. The focus is primarily on the coupling between the qubits using the quantum Fisher information as the measured parameter. Some results on estimating the qubit-cavity detuning parameter are also presented. We investigate the scaling of the uncertainty in the estimate of the qubit-cavity coupling with the number of qubits and for different initial states of the qubits that act as the quantum probe. As initial probe states, we consider Dicke states with varying excitation numbers, the GHZ state, and separable X-polarized states. It is shown that in the strong coupling regime, i.e., when the coupling between the qubits and the cavity is greater than the decay parameters of both the qubits and the cavity, Dicke states with a large excitation number can achieve the Heisenberg limit, with the precision scaling improving as the excitation number increases. A particularly intriguing finding of our study is that in the weak coupling regime, as well as in situations where either the qubit or cavity decay parameters exceed the coupling, the separable X-polarized state is the best in terms of scaling and is even able to achieve the Heisenberg limit in these lossy regimes for the range of N considered.
items.author: Quinn Langfitt, Zain H. Saleem, Michael A. Perlin, Tian Zhong et al.

items.title: On the representations of a family of pointed Hopf algebras
items.summary: We study the representations of a family of pointed Hopf algebras 𝒜 λ , μ which arise as 2-parameter deformations of the Fomin–Kirillov algebra ℱ𝒦 3 . We classify the simple modules and their projective covers. We observe that our results are fundamentally different according to the shape of the Hopf cocycle involved in the deformation.
items.author: Agustín García Iglesias, Alfio Antonio Rodriguez

items.title: Quantum Metropolis Sampling via Weak Measurement
items.summary: Gibbs sampling is a crucial computational technique used in physics, statistics, and many other scientific fields. For classical Hamiltonians, the most commonly used Gibbs sampler is the Metropolis algorithm, known for having the Gibbs state as its unique fixed point. For quantum Hamiltonians, designing provably correct Gibbs samplers has been more challenging. [TOV+11] introduced a novel method that uses quantum phase estimation (QPE) and the Marriot-Watrous rewinding technique to mimic the classical Metropolis algorithm for quantum Hamiltonians. The analysis of their algorithm relies upon the use of a boosted and shift-invariant version of QPE which may not exist [CKBG23]. Recent efforts to design quantum Gibbs samplers take a very different approach and are based on simulating Davies generators [CKBG23,CKG23,RWW23,DLL24]. Currently, these are the only provably correct Gibbs samplers for quantum Hamiltonians. We revisit the inspiration for the Metropolis-style algorithm of [TOV+11] and incorporate weak measurement to design a conceptually simple and provably correct quantum Gibbs sampler, with the Gibbs state as its approximate unique fixed point. Our method uses a Boosted QPE which takes the median of multiple runs of QPE, but we do not require the shift-invariant property. In addition, we do not use the Marriott-Watrous rewinding technique which simplifies the algorithm significantly.
items.author: Jiaqing Jiang, Sandy Irani

items.title: Optimal Quantum Purity Amplification: A Top-Down Approach to Error Suppression via Symmetry and Reversibility
items.summary: Quantum purity amplification (QPA) provides a novel approach to counteracting the pervasive noise that degrades quantum states. We present the optimal QPA protocol for general quantum systems and global noise, resolving a two-decade open problem. Under strong depolarization, our protocol achieves an exponential reduction in sample complexity over the best-known methods. We provide an efficient implementation of the protocol based on generalized quantum phase estimation. Additionally, we introduce SWAPNET, a sparse and shallow circuit that enables QPA for near-term experiments. Simulations in both digital and analog quantum settings, along with experiments on superconducting quantum processors, confirm the protocol's robustness and practical utility. Our findings suggest that QPA could improve the performance of quantum information processing tasks, particularly in the context of Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices, where reducing the effect of noise with limited resources is critical.
items.author: Zhaoyi Li, Honghao Fu, Takuya Isogawa, Caio Silva et al.

items.title: Symmetry in Thermal Fluid Sciences and Energy Applications
items.summary: Symmetry is a fundamental notion in thermal-fluid sciences and energy applications and an important tool for understanding the properties of complex systems. Thermal and fluid processes are applied in several modern energy use technologies, basically consisting of the complex multidimensional interaction of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics. A comprehensive analysis involves vector and scalar quantities in the flow field, where symmetry is highly considered in order to simplify geometric parameters. These requirements therefore are also applied to experimental techniques, and the interconnection between experimental analysis and numerical simulation of processes is an important field. Thus, there is a wide range of symmetry solutions for this research area, the results of which contribute to the development of science and fast information for decision-making in industry.
items.author: Nattan Roberto Caetano

items.title: Computational Study of Entangled Two-Photon Absorption in Organic Dyes
items.summary: Abstract Entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) offers advantages for quantum spectroscopy, including linear scaling with photon flux and reduced photodamage, yet distinguishing it from competing one-photon processes remains experimentally challenging. We present a predictive framework based on time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) that clarifies the mechanisms shaping ETPA spectra in organic chromophores. Using rhodamine 6G and zinc tetraphenylporphyrin, we show that nondegenerate photon pairs enhance ETPA intensity when one photon approaches resonance with a one-photon absorption (OPA) transition. We clarify that this enhancement is a near-resonant, sum-over-states effect shared with classical two-photon absorption rather than a quantum advantage; entanglement instead acts through the joint spectral amplitude as a correlation-induced weighting that redistributes intensity and reduces to classical TPA in the appropriate limit. Despite the typical TD-DFT blue shift (∼0.5 eV), the method predicts spectral trends over energy ranges beyond those accessible by spontaneous parametric down-conversion, guiding experimental design.
items.source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
items.author: David R. Graupner, Matthias Kizmann, Hari Kumar Yadalam, Raju Bhai KC et al.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction for constant-excitation stabilizer codes under coherent noise
items.summary: Abstract Collective coherent (CC) noise poses challenges for fault-tolerant error correction (FTEC), as it is not captured by conventional stochastic noise models. Constant-excitation (CE) codes are inherently immune to CC errors, but a fault-tolerant framework for operating these codes under circuit-level noise has not yet been established. Here, we develop an FTEC framework for CE CSS codes based on dual-rail concatenation. We show that conventional transversal CNOT gates violate the CE constraint and develop CE-preserving logical CNOT gates together with modified Shor- and Steane-type syndrome extraction schemes using zero-controlled NOT gates and CE-compatible ancilla states. We further develop an extended stabilizer simulation algorithm that tracks both stochastic and CC noise. Using this framework, we identify small distance-3 CE CSS codes demonstrate that the [[14, 1, 3]] code maintains robust performance under coherent noise. Our results establish a fault-tolerant framework for CE codes under circuit-level noise and demonstrate their potential for quantum processors affected by CC noise.
items.author: Ching–Yi Lai, Pei-Hao Liou, Yingkai Ouyang

items.title: Quantum theory of electrically levitated nanoparticle-ion systems: Motional dynamics and sympathetic cooling
items.summary: We develop the theory describing the quantum coupled dynamics of the center-of-mass motion of a nanoparticle and an ensemble of ions co-trapped in a dual-frequency linear Paul trap. We first derive analytical expressions for the motional frequencies and classical trajectories of both nanoparticle and ions. We then derive a quantum master equation for the ion-nanoparticle system and quantify the sympathetic cooling of the nanoparticle motion enabled by its Coulomb coupling to a continuously Doppler-cooled ion. We predict that motional cooling down to sub-kelvin temperatures is achievable in state-of-the-art experiments even in the absence of motional feedback and in the presence of micromotion. We then extend our analysis to an ensemble of $N$ ions, predicting a linear increase of the cooling rate as a function of $N$ and motional cooling of the nanoparticle down to tenths of millikelvin in current experimental platforms. Our work establishes the theoretical toolbox needed to explore the ion-assisted preparation of non-Gaussian motional states of levitated nanoparticles.
items.author: Saurabh Gupta, Bernard Faulend, Dmitry S. Bykov, Tracy E. Northup et al.

items.title: No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs
items.summary: Constructing ensembles of circuits which efficiently approximate the Haar measure over various groups is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, with breakthrough recent results showing that for the unitary group this can be achieved with depths scaling logarithmically in the system size. Here we prove that, for groups G possessing an invariant state $${G}^{\otimes k}\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle=\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle$$ satisfying certain conditions on its entanglement structure, no subset of G consisting of sublinear-depth one-dimensional circuits with constant-locality gates can form an approximate k-design over G. More generally, on a D-dimensional lattice of side-length n, our results imply that such group designs require depths scaling at least as n1/D. Among other examples, we show that there is a constant separation between the maximum depth and gate counts for which no circuit can approximate even the second moment of random matchgate circuits, and those required to implement the matchgate Haar distribution exactly. Finally, we relax the assumption of working with local gates, and prove the impossibility of obtaining approximate designs over G using any circuit comprised of a sublinear number of gates generated by Pauli strings. Significant effort has been spent to find low-depth constructions of random unitaries that appear Haar-random to a restricted observer, and earlier works showed logarithmic-depth approximate designs over the full unitary group using local random circuits. In this paper, the authors provide a general criterion ruling out shallow designs on a wide variety of groups.
items.author: Maxwell West, Diego García-Martín, N. L. Diaz, M. Cerezo et al.

items.title: Scalable generation of macroscopic Fock states exceeding 10,000 photons
items.summary: The scalable preparation of bosonic quantum states with macroscopic excitations poses a fundamental challenge in quantum technologies, limited by control complexity and photon-loss rates that severely constrain prior theoretical and experimental efforts to merely dozens of excitations per mode. Here, based on the duality of the quantum state evolution in Fock state space and the optical wave-function propagation in a waveguide array, we introduce a Kerr-engineered multi-lens protocol in a single bosonic mode to deterministically generate Fock states exceeding $10,000$ photons. By optimizing phase and displacement operations across lens groups, our approach compensates for non-paraxial aberrations, achieving fidelities above $73\%$ in numerical simulations for photon numbers up to $N=100,000$. Counterintuitively, the protocol's execution time scales as $N^{-1/2}$ with the target photon number $N$, exhibiting robustness against the photon loss. Our framework enables exploration of quantum-to-classical transitions of giant Fock states, paving the way for advanced quantum metrology with significant quantum gains, and error-corrected quantum information processing in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
items.author: Ming Li, Weizhou Cai, Ziyue Hua, Yifang Xu et al.

items.title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
items.summary: Quantum channel tomography (also known as quantum process tomography) is a fundamental task in quantum information and quantum computing, aiming to learn the full description of an unknown quantum channel from black-box queries. For channels with input dimension $d_1$, output dimension $d_2$, and Kraus rank at most $r$, [CGO+26] identifies the dilation rate $τ=rd_2/d_1\geq 1$ as a key parameter governing a Heisenberg-to-classical transition in query complexity. While the optimal bounds in the boundary regime ($τ=1$) and the away-from-boundary regime ($τ\geq 1+Ω(1)$) are now known, the precise behavior in the near-boundary regime ($1<τ<1+o(1)$) has remained unresolved. In this paper, we close this gap, thereby fully settling the query complexity of quantum channel tomography. Specifically, we show that the query complexity is - $Ω(rd_1d_2/\varepsilon^2)$ for diamond norm error $\varepsilon$, matching the upper bound by [MB26, CGO+26], - $Θ(d_1^2/\varepsilon+\min\{(τ-1)d_1^2,(τ-1)^2d_1^2d_2^2\}/\varepsilon^2)$ for Choi trace norm error $\varepsilon$. Our results reveal two qualitatively different forms of the Heisenberg-to-classical transition. For diamond norm tomography, the Heisenberg scaling disappears suddenly as soon as $τ$ leaves the boundary regime. In contrast, Choi trace norm tomography exhibits a gradual transition from Heisenberg to classical scaling as $τ$ moves from the boundary regime to the away-from-boundary regime.
items.author: Kean Chen, Aadil Oufkir

items.title: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach
items.summary: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. The expansion coefficients are modular integrals of modular-flowed vacuum correlators. Our formula provides a systematic treatment of arbitrary multi-point sectors, and recovers known results on two-point sector derived from replica methods. The full two-point sector resums into a modular integral of the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, with an effective temperature depending on ball configuration and modular time. We compute the expansion explicitly in CFTs. In two-dimensional Ising CFT, using analytic reductions and multidimensional numerical integration, we obtain the first ten radial orders in the long-distance expansion, which involve sphere correlators with up to twenty spin insertions. The truncated expansion agrees well with lattice data at finite separation, and approximately satisfies crossing symmetry. Analytic calculations also reproduce known expansion coefficients for 2d free compact boson at self-dual radius and its current sector, as well as for free scalars in higher dimensions.
items.author: Hewei Frederic Jia

items.title: Lee-Yang theorems for $q$-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK
items.summary: We show that the vacuum partition function of the $q$-deformed oscillator \[ L_q(z):= \langle0|e^{zT_q}|0\rangle, \qquad T_q := \mathsf{a}_q + \mathsf{a}_q^* \] satisfies the Lee-Yang property, i.e., all zeros of $L_q$ lie on the imaginary line for all $q\in[-1, 1)$, proving the conjectures of Okuyama'23. Using the connection between $q$-deformed oscillators and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian in the doubly-scaled regime, we show that the annealed SYK partition function satisfies the Lee-Yang property in the thermodynamic limit, that is, all of its Fisher zeros are on the imaginary axis. As a result, we show that the quenched SYK partition function admits a zero-free strip of constant width with high probability, rigorously complementing the large$-k$ replica calculations of Zlokapa and Kiani'26. We show the imaginary-rootedness of $L_q$ by expressing $\varphi_q(z):= L_q(\mathbf{i} z)$ as a locally uniform limit of ``$q$-deformed'' matching polynomials and then showing that those $q$-deformed polynomials are real-rooted. This establishes that $\varphi_q$ is real-rooted, and in fact belongs to the \emph{Laguerre-Pólya} class. The real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials yields novel log-concavity relations on the \emph{$q$-deformed matching moments} \[M_\ell(q):= \sum_{π\in\mathcal{P}_2(2\ell)}q^{\operatorname{cr}(π)}.\] We show the real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials by using the Touchard--Riordan formula to derive a partial differential equation relating their $q$-derivatives to their $z$-derivatives, and then analyzing the resulting motion of their roots.
items.author: Arpon Basu, Siddhant Midha

items.title: Spacetime Emergence in the Memory of a Learning Agent
items.summary: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. We train a model-based reinforcement-learning agent to maximize the quantum mutual information between localized quantum probes interacting with a quantum field in Minkowski spacetime, without directly providing it with information regarding the spacetime metric or causal structure. In learning to accomplish this task, the reinforcement-learning agent constructs an internal predictive model whose planner develops the characteristic null structure of spacetime, allowing us to reconstruct the causal structure of the Minkowski metric with high accuracy. Within this task, spacetime geometry is obtained from an agent's successful predictions and actions, providing a first step toward showing that spacetime concepts emerge from operational quantum experience.
items.author: Philip A. LeMaitre, T. Rick Perche

items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.summary: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions as a route to low-power temperature sensors while providing insight into carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions.
items.author: Sungjae Hong, Jeffrey A. Ivie, Tzu-Ming Lu, Christopher R. Allemang

items.title: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy
items.summary: Scientific applications of free electrons, such as in electron microscopes and particle accelerators, are limited by the brightness of available electron sources. Accelerators can use phase space cooling to surpass these source limitations, whereas electron microscopes can only rely on particle filtering to increase beam coherence at the cost of reduced brightness. We show that strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures makes it possible to achieve single-pass stochastic cooling inside an electron microscope for a lossless improvement of longitudinal emittance. This approach is laser-free and compatible with normal CW operation of electron microscopes. We derive a fully quantum mechanical model of stochastic cooling valid in the strong coupling regime, finding an analytic asymptotic formula for the optimal cooled energy spread $σ_{E_f}\simeq0.88(\hbarω)^{2/3}σ_{E_0}^{1/3}$, with $\hbar ω$ the cooling photon energy and $σ_{E_0}$ the initial energy spread. Numerical simulations confirm that the energy spread reduction is reflected in an increase in the purity of the electron's quantum state and a reduction of the longitudinal phase space area. Our work paves a path towards even brighter beams for electron microscopy, promising higher image quality, enhanced spectral resolution, and a route to reaching fundamental quantum limits on electron beam phase space area.
items.author: River Robles, Peter Hommelhoff

items.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
items.summary: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.
items.author: Mohamed Nomeir, Sennur Ulukus

items.title: Unifying entanglement and nonclassicality via the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum
items.summary: Entanglement and nonclassicality are two fundamental features of quantum mechanics which serve as resources in quantum information processing tasks and are tightly connected by two-mode mixing. In this work, we show that the connection between entanglement and nonclassicality extends well beyond the two-mode mixing setting by considering the case of arbitrary multimode Gaussian evolutions. Using the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum as our main technical tool to quantify single-mode phase-space nonclassicality, we derive sufficient conditions for a single-mode state to generate NPT entanglement after a multimode Gaussian unitary evolution, which both tighten and generalize existing criteria. As an application, we obtain simple single-mode protocols for quantitatively testing the entanglement structure of multimode quantum states over arbitrary bipartitions. Our results identify the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum as a powerful tool for investigating fundamental properties of bosonic quantum states.
items.author: Massimo Frigerio, Zacharie Van Herstraeten, Hania Herbi, Jack Davis et al.

items.title: Quantum tomography on Schwartz space
items.summary: In this work we show that standard results in quantum tomography, which are typically proven in the context of Hilbert spaces, can analogously be established in the theory of Schwartz spaces. In particular, we will see that quantum states are equivalently characterized by their Wigner function, the characteristic of their Wigner function, and the probability distributions for a family of linear combinations of position and momentum. Physically, the latter can be understood as the evolution of its probability distribution in position over time under, for example, free or harmonic evolution. The result is obtained with techniques that are more accessible to a physicist audience, and shows that, at least for tomography results, the full structure of Hilbert spaces is not necessary.
items.author: Tobias Thrien, Gabriele Carcassi, David Carfì, Christine A. Aidala

items.title: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
items.summary: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound $\varepsilon$ on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of \textit{bad} seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce $δ$-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability $\left(\frac{\varepsilon}δ\right)^2$. This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of $k$ rounds except with failure probability $\big(\frac{(2k-1)\varepsilon}δ\big)^2$. Moreover, we extend the gene
items.author: Asker Friis Bach, Isabel Moreno Babuglia, Jonatan Bohr Brask

items.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
items.summary: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $π$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.
items.author: Yves Rottstaedt, Andrei I. Pavlovm Alexander Shnirman, Yuval Gefen, Bernd Rosenow

items.title: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence
items.summary: Experiments with cryogenic beams of hydrogen isotopes (hydrogen (H), deuterium (D), and tritium (T)) can be used to study quantum reflection from solid dielectric mirrors. Most dielectric surfaces carry trapped electric charges whose field polarizes the incident atom. We study theoretically how such charges, distributed randomly, in clusters, with compensation over a finite length, or in order, change specular reflection and diffuse scattering of H, D, and T at grazing incidence on typical dielectric mirrors (SiO$_2$/Si and MgF$_2$), for longitudinal velocities of 100--300~m/s and normal velocities of 3--100~cm/s which might become available soon in grazing incidence experiments. Starting from the exact coupled-channel equations, we show that the specular wave feels only the laterally averaged polarization potential, which is fixed by the structure factor of the charges and, for uncorrelated charges, is an inverse-square tail $-C_2/z^2$. The exact solution replaces the linear threshold law $1-\Rr\propto\vperp$ by the fractional power $\vperp^{2ν}$, $ν=(1/4-ζ)^{1/2}$, with the coupling $ζ\propto C_2$; for weak coupling, this appears as a logarithmic velocity dependence, and for $ζ>1/4$, the reflection coefficient oscillates log-periodically. At the surface charge density of $10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$, absorption increases by up to 26\% for SiO$_2$/Si and by a factor of two to three for MgF$_2$; the effect increases with atomic mass, saturates for compensated charges, and is accompanied by diffuse scattering below $10^{-3}$ of charge-induced loss. We also formulate the condition of complete absorption at the solid surface.
items.author: A. Yu. Voronin, V. V. Nesvizhevsky

items.title: Unifying quantum smoothing theories with extended retrodiction
items.summary: Estimating the state of an open quantum system monitored over time requires incorporating information from past measurements (filtering) and, for improved accuracy, also from future measurements (smoothing). While classical smoothing is well understood within a Bayesian framework, its quantum generalization has been challenging, leading to distinct and seemingly incompatible approaches. In this work, we demonstrate that quantum state smoothing hinges on a uniquely quantum feature: the fundamental dependence of retrodiction on prior correlations. We introduce auxiliary systems into the prior to represent specified correlations formed during preparation and evolution, and formulate quantum state smoothing as extended Bayesian retrodiction. This framework identifies previous approaches as different choices of the extended prior, and naturally extends it to other choices that have not been considered before. We also give an information-theoretic characterization of the choices of prior, in terms of the average entropy of the smoothed states. Our results establish quantum state smoothing as a fundamentally retrodictive process just like classical smoothing, with proper quantum features clearly identified.
items.author: Mingxuan Liu, Ge Bai, Valerio Scarani

items.title: Accelerating noisy variational quantum algorithms with physics-informed denoising networks
items.summary: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum computing, but are severely limited by hardware noise and the substantial circuit overhead required for error mitigation methods such as Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE). We propose a Physics-Informed Denoising Network (PIDN) that reduces the cost of ZNE by learning a surrogate model of its optimization dynamics. By viewing the variational update as a trajectory in the parameter space, PIDN is trained to reproduce ZNE-mitigated expectation values and gradient directions while incorporating a physics-informed loss that preserves the gradient descent dynamics. Once trained, PIDN replaces repeated multi-noise evaluations with denoised expectation and gradient estimation directly from the current noisy observation and the historical trajectory, significantly reducing circuit executions. We benchmark the approach on the quantum approximate optimization algorithm for 3-regular graphs, Sherrington-Kirkpatrick, and transverse-field Ising models, as well as the variational quantum eigensolver for LiH, BeH$_2$ and H$_2$O. Across all tasks, PIDN attains performance comparable to ZNE, while reducing the number of circuit executions by a factor of approximately 4 to 6. Gradient cosine similarity with ZNE remains above 0.95 throughout training. Robustness analysis shows that PIDN fails only when ZNE itself becomes unreliable, and ablation studies confirm the necessity of the physics-informed loss for maintaining directional consistency. We further find that PIDN tracks optimization dynamics most accurately when the effective loss landscape retains strong low-frequency structure. These results establish PIDN as a scalable, resource-efficient strategy for noise-resilient variational optimization in the noisy intermediate-
items.author: Jie Liu, Xin Wang

items.title: Unconditional authentication in quantum key distribution via hybrid entangled physical unclonable functions
items.summary: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) enables Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) key exchange, robust even against future quantum computing threats. However, a fundamental limitation of QKD is the requirement for an authenticated classical channel, which necessitates a pre-shared secret key. In this work, we address this challenge by adopting a Hybrid Entangled Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) protocol for authentication. We demonstrate that this PUF-based method generates an ITS initial key under minimal explicit hardware assumptions. This approach allows us to experimentally perform a fully ITS-authenticated entanglement-based QKD protocol that relies solely on such assumptions, effectively eliminating the need for pre-shared secrets. This represents a significant step towards the practical realization of quantum network protocols using lightweight, readily available hardware assumptions, without weakening security guarantees.
items.author: Nicolas Laurent-Puig, Mina Doosti, Adriano Innocenzi, Eleni Diamanti

items.title: Three-form dark energy: constraints and multi-probe comparison with ΛCDM
items.author: Mariam Bouhmadi-López, a Hsu-Wen Chiang, Carlos G. Boiza, Javier Ortega del Río et al.

items.title: Beyond the ground state: a spin-resolved reaction network for oxygen evolution reaction on NiOOH
items.author: Ilia M. Odud, Vitaly G. Kiselev, Sergey V. Levchenko

items.title: High-accuracy prediction of Kβ/Kα intensity ratios via explainable stacked-ensemble learning : A web-based computational tool
items.summary: The Kβ/Kα intensity ratios are critical parameters that quantitatively characterize atomic shell transition dynamics and radiative branching probabilities. In this study, we systematically evaluated the capability of machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict these ratios, as well as their advantages over traditional theoretical models (such as Scofield and semi-empirical calculations). A large dataset comprising 2124 experimental measurements compiled from the literature, covering elements with atomic numbers (Z) from 11 to 96, was structured to include more than ten variables, such as atomic number, sample form, excitation source, detector type, and energy resolution. Missing observations were imputed using the multivariate imputation by chained equations (MICE) method in the R programming language. Categorical variables were one-hot encoded, and the data were split into an 80% training set and a 20% test set. Seven heterogeneous individual models (RF, XGBoost, Cubist, SVR, GPR, BRNN, and GLMNET) were constructed, along with seven different stacking combinations derived from them. Following 10×10-fold cross-validation, the highest accuracy was achieved by the stacked model using a BRNN meta-learner (RMSE = 0.009; R2 = 0.973). This model reduced the test error of the Scofield theory by nearly 48% and performed significantly better according to the Diebold–Mariano test (p < 0.001). SHAP analysis revealed that atomic number is the primary determinant, while sample purity and excitation source have secondary yet physically consistent effects. Furthermore, an online R/Shiny-based calculator enhances the practical applicability of the method by enabling users to input their experimental parameters and receive instantaneous Kβ/Kα predictions. items.author: C.M. Yeşilkanat, E. Cengi̇z, Abdelhalim KAHOUL, A. Zidi et al.

items.title: Quantizing Gravitational Fields with an Entropy-Corrected Action Principle
items.summary: A variational framework for the quantization of gravitational fields is developed based on an extension of the stationary action principle. Within this framework, the Wheeler-DeWitt equation for the gravitational wave functional is recovered without assuming operator promotion of the canonical momentum, thus avoiding the ambiguity of operator ordering in canonical quantization. The derivation is based on three main ingredients. First, motivated by information-theoretic considerations, the classical stationary action principle is generalized by incorporating a correction term constructed from the relative entropy associated with field fluctuations. Second, an ensemble formulation on superspace is enhanced to incorporate this entropy correction. Third, the formalism is further refined to provide a unified treatment of quantization and constraints, thereby addressing the long-standing ambiguity concerning the ordering of quantization and constraint reduction. The framework is then applied to gravitational fields coupled to a massless scalar field. Using an emergent time parameter defined via the rate equation of the gravitational fields, a Schrodinger equation for the scalar-field wave functional is recovered, supplemented by an additional quantum correction term suppressed at order $G\hbar^2$. Finally, we comment on possible connections between the notion of relative entropy employed here and holographic dualities in quantum gravity.
items.author: Jianhao M. Yang

items.title: Efficient multi-basis quantum position verification secure against generalized adversaries
items.summary: Abstract Quantum position verification (QPV) enables multiple verifiers to certify a prover’s location using quantum communication and physical assumptions. With experimental demonstrations of QPV becoming increasingly feasible, enhancing the practicality and security of QPV protocols is more important than ever. In this work, we make three key contributions toward this goal. First, we introduce a robust QPV protocol in which the verifier’s state preparation is independent of channel loss, improving reliability in real-world conditions. Second, we refine existing security analysis techniques to bolster protocol resilience against experimental imperfections. Third, we identify and address some implicit assumptions present in existing security analyses, providing a framework to eliminate such assumptions. Additionally, as an example of QPV application beyond location verification, we illustrate how QPV can be leveraged for authenticating classical communication in quantum key distribution.
items.author: Wen Yu Kon, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Kaushik Chakraborty, Charles Ci Wen Lim

items.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
items.summary: Abstract Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. We identify individual hyperfine-Zeeman-rotational components of the fundamental vibrational transition of the nitrogen molecular ion, $${{{{{\rm{N}}}}}}_{2}^{+}$$ N 2 + , and perform coherent population transfer between energy levels. Our work opens up new perspectives for precision molecular spectroscopy, for high-fidelity qubits encoded in the rotational-vibrational motion of molecules, for precise infrared molecular clocks and for searches for new physics.
items.author: Aleksandr Shlykov, Meissa L. Diouf, Richard Karl, Mikolaj Roguski et al.

items.title: A Quantum-HPC Hybrid Workflow for Reaction-Center Electronic Dynamics: Application to a Cytochrome P450-Inspired Iron-Complex Model
items.summary: Abstract We introduce population-transfer dynamics as a practical validation observable for active-state-derived reduced Hamiltonians in multistate reaction-center chemistry. In transition-metal systems, missing couplings or configurations can compromise the reliability of reduced active space models along a reaction coordinate, even when the overall spectrum is reproduced reasonably well. Using a cytochrome P450-inspired Fe-complex model, we construct a reaction-coordinate-dependent effective Hamiltonian from state-averaged complete active-space self-consistent field (SA-CASSCF) calculations, map it to a quantum circuit representation suitable for current hardware, and propagate the dynamics from the reactant-side ground state. At the spectrum level, the reduced Hamiltonian reproduces the SA-CASSCF reference with an RMS deviation of 0.030 eV and a maximum absolute deviation of 0.143 eV. As a dynamics-based diagnostic, the product-manifold population pP(t) identifies a pronounced near-degeneracy window around x ≈ 0.3, where state mixing is strongest; specifically, computed from classical exact time evolution reaches 0.488 at x = 0.3 after 10 fs, compared with 7.26 × 10–2 at x = 0.2 and 5.90 × 10–3 at x = 0.0. To render the workflow executable on current trapped-ion hardware, we quantify the NISQ-relevant trade-off between dynamical fidelity and circuit resources through coupling pruning and first-order Trotterization. A coupling cutoff of ε = 0.02 eV reduces the nonzero coupling set from 32 to 7 while preserving the dominant transfer pathways, and a Trotter step number of M = 30 provides the best practical operating point among the tested values. items.author: Jonathan Washburn

items.title: A comprehensive review of computational strategies in the rational design of biosensors based on allosteric transcription factors for pollutant detection
items.summary: Allosteric transcription factor (aTF)-based biosensors are powerful analytical tools for the detection of different analytes such as environmental pollutants and are widely used in medical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. These biosensors rely on ligand-induced conformational changes in transcription factors that regulate gene expression, thereby positioning them as low-cost, sensitive and selective components in biosensor design. In recent times, computational biology and chemistry techniques such as homology modelling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy perturbation (FEP), enhanced sampling techniques and machine learning have been widely employed in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors. With these methods, the structures of proteins could be predicted, the ligand-binding pockets could be identified and characterized, the interactions therein could be analyzed and binding affinities could be predicted. Also, the conformational dynamics, allosteric and transition pathways, free energy landscapes, relative binding free energies of the ligand-aTF complexes can be predicted. Taken together, these can facilitate the engineering of aTFs with improved sensitivity and specificity. Therefore, this review highlights the individual and complementary roles of these computational techniques in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors and discusses the recent advances, current limitations and future directions in the design of next-generation aTF-based biosensors.
items.author: Oluwatoba Emmanuel Oyeneyin

items.title: Quantum Wavefront Stabilization and Topological Optical Regularization: Resolving Phase Discontinuity via Trans-Planckian Horizon Lock Mechanics
items.summary: This treatise delivers the definitive mathematical physics formulation to resolve the problem of optical wavefront layer discontinuities, phase factor anomalies, and singular photon information dissipation gradients within quantum-applied continuum architectures. Traditional optical propagation and wave-routing algorithms suffer from severe mathematical breakdown due to localized computational entropy spikes under extreme diffractive constraints. Operating within the functional infrastructure of Trans-Planckian Horizon Lock Mechanics (TPHLM), we resolve these material instabilities by executing a rigorous multi-loop tensor regularization under the global metric scale factor of the Khandey Causal Invariant Constant (K_J = 2.02 x 10^26 m). This architecture satisfies absolute diffeomorphism Ward-Khandey identities, cancels trace field anomalies, and ensures a deterministic 0.0000000000000000% floating-point error baseline, optimized for high-performance exascale computing arrays.
